The bank also increased its holdings in Bitcoin treasury company Strategy by 36% to nearly 849,000 shares, worth about $131 million at the end of Q3.
Laurore, which lists a Hong Kong business address in its SEC filing, reduced its IBIT holdings by 33%, cutting its position by 1.6 million shares to 3.25 million, worth about $154 million by the end of Q3. articles.title: Microsoft 365 Outage Hits Outlook, Teams as Recovery Falters
articles.text:
Microsoft 365 outage hits Outlook email and Teams calendars worldwide
Microsoft began a wider patch rollout Friday as the outage disrupted government email and Microsoft 365 connectors in ChatGPT and Claude.
A global Microsoft 365 outage continued into Friday, disrupting Outlook email and some Teams features.
Microsoft said in a 7:25 am UTC update that a patch had improved stability on some servers and that it was working to deploy the fix more widely. The update, republished by the University of Pennsylvania, gave no timetable for restoration.
The outage began Thursday, leaving some users unable to access their Exchange Online mailboxes. Microsoft said a process that handles secure connection became overloaded, causing affected servers to stop processing requests.
The company said it attempted to restore services by restarting infrastructure, redirecting network traffic and expanding server capacity. Microsoft said there was no indication of a security breach.
The outage also affected features in Microsoft Copilot and Defender for Office 365. In Teams, users had trouble scheduling meetings and sending invitations. Microsoft said most Teams calls and chats continued to work.
Businesses and government agencies worldwide use Microsoft 365 for email and scheduling. Microsoft reported more than 450 million paid commercial seats for the suite in an October filing. Exchange Online hosts the mailboxes and calendars those organizations use, and outside apps, including AI assistants, rely on the same service to retrieve that data when users connect their work accounts.
OpenAI reported errors in ChatGPT’s Microsoft 365 connector. Anthropic said the outage caused most email, calendar and search requests through Claude’s Microsoft 365 connector to fail.
The US Court of Appeals for the Tenth Circuit said its clerk’s office could neither send nor receive email for much of Thursday. Japan’s Finance Ministry said it was unable to receive email on Friday and Singapore’s Government Technology Agency told CNA that government email was among systems affected.
Related: Amsterdam protesters break into Microsoft data center construction site: Report

articles.title: Nvidia Employees Push Board to Bring Back Jensen Huang: Report - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- An internal Nvidia "suggestion box" post urging the board to consider employee sentiment has drawn more than 1,600 comments, according to Wired.
- Several commenters asked the board to bring back former CEO Jensen Huang, and one employee sent a companywide email demanding transparency over his exit.
- Huang resigned on Thursday after reports of relationships with a suspected Chinese spy and an Nvidia executive; Reuters has since reported a third relationship.
Some Nvidia employees are calling on the company's board to bring back Jensen Huang, days after he resigned as CEO following reports of extramarital relationships, according to internal correspondence reviewed by Wired.
An internal "suggestion box" post, submitted by a longtime engineer prior to Huang's resignation, urged the board to take employee sentiment into account before acting, Wired reported. It has since drawn more than 1,600 comments, several of which asked the board to find a way to reinstate Huang. "If you believe in the mission, bring back THE boss," one anonymous commenter wrote.
The post also called on the board to share the findings of its investigation with staff and to formally seek their views on Huang continuing as CEO. One employee went further, sending a companywide email demanding transparency about Huang's exit and declaring: "I stand by Jensen."
In the hours following Huang's departure, some two dozen Nvidia employees posted supportive messages on LinkedIn, while Wired said it could not find any employee posts backing his departure. The engineer behind the suggestion box post declined to comment, and Nvidia and its new board chair, Harvey Jones, did not immediately respond to the outlet.
Huang's exit
Huang resigned as Nvidia's president, CEO and a board member on Thursday, ending a 33-year tenure at the company he co-founded. Chief financial officer Colette Kress is serving as interim CEO, and Jones, a former CEO of Synopsys, became the board's first chair. Nvidia did not give a reason for the resignation.
Huang told staff on Sunday that he had been "unfaithful" to his wife, without naming anyone.
The New York Times had reported in October that surveillance of Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, indicated that she had developed a "close relationship" with the Nvidia CEO. Per the Times, U.S. officials concluded she was a Chinese intelligence asset, while the Financial Times reported that a U.S. memo said the two had been romantically involved. China has denied that she is a spy.
Alice Huang was CEO and chair of Megaspeed, a Singapore-based Nvidia customer, and was investigated by Singapore police over possible false declarations relating to the company's server purchases, the country's Ministry of Home Affairs said on Thursday. She was not investigated for espionage, it said.
Police found insufficient evidence that she had committed any offenses, but concluded she had knowingly given them inaccurate information to downplay her role at Megaspeed, according to the ministry. She was issued a stern warning, left Singapore in February and was barred from returning. Investigations into Megaspeed and six other people are ongoing.
Alice Huang is now living in Beijing with the knowledge of security officials, Bloomberg reported, citing a person familiar with the matter. Attorney General Todd Blanche said on Thursday that the Justice Department had not yet concluded whether Huang was a spy, and that the FBI was investigating the reports, according to Reuters, which was unable to reach her for comment.
On Wednesday, the Times reported that Jensen Huang had also had a relationship with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia's vice president of health care, who reported directly to him. Powell has not commented.
On Thursday, Reuters reported, citing two people familiar with the matter, that Huang had an intimate relationship with a second Nvidia employee, whom it did not name. Nvidia declined to comment to Reuters, and Huang and a representative for the board did not respond. Huang has not commented on the reports since his Sunday email, according to Wired.
Support outside Nvidia
The calls inside Nvidia echo criticism of the board's decision from tech and crypto figures. Binance co-founder Changpeng "CZ" Zhao called it a mistake for Nvidia to let Huang resign, while Elon Musk said hiring him would be "an honor."
Huang still faces scrutiny in Washington. Congressional committees have asked him to sit for a closed-door interview on December 1 and to testify at a Senate hearing on December 3, as lawmakers examine Nvidia's chip exports to China.
He and Nvidia also face a proposed shareholder class action over his alleged ties to Alice Huang.
Nvidia reports quarterly earnings on Tuesday, the first under Kress.

articles.title: Bitcoin Price Sinks Below $70K as Crypto Sentiment Weakens
articles.text:
Bitcoin slides below $70K amid thin liquidity, ETF outflows
Bitcoin fell below $70,000 as crypto sentiment hit its lowest level in more than four months, with analysts warning of institutional outflows, thinning liquidity and elevated leverage.
Bitcoin fell below $70,000 on Friday, extending its recent decline as investor sentiment deteriorated amid institutional outflows, tightening liquidity and broader macroeconomic pressures.
Bitcoin (BTC) is trading at $68,607.23 at the time of writing, down 9.2% in the last week, according to CoinGecko.
The decline coincided with a sharp decline in market sentiment. The Crypto Fear & Greed Index fell to 20 on Friday, its lowest reading in more than four months, putting it in “extreme fear.” The index last reached that level on July 8.
Vikram Subburaj, CEO of crypto exchange Giottus, attributed Bitcoin’s weakness to institutional outflows, tightening crypto liquidity and expectations of a December Federal Reserve interest rate hike. “Investors should avoid chasing short-term dips or using excessive leverage,” he said.
In a Friday report, 10x Research highlighted Bitcoin’s divergence from US equities. Between Nov. 5 and Nov. 12, Bitcoin declined 5.9% while the Nasdaq 100 gained 6.4%, suggesting the cryptocurrency was responding more to rising Treasury yields and a stronger US dollar than to technology stocks.
The research firm said Bitcoin was increasingly trading alongside gold, which fell 5.5% over the same period, as the US 10-year Treasury yield climbed above 5%.
Meanwhile, institutional trading platform Talos also warned that thin liquidity and elevated leverage could amplify market volatility. Its weekly report showed Bitcoin order-book depth across major exchanges fell to $72 million on Nov. 9, roughly 33% below normal levels.
“Liquidity remains thin while leverage stays elevated, leaving the market vulnerable to sharp moves in either direction,” said Tanay Ved, senior research associate at Talos. “A rebuild in order-book depth and a turn in capital flows would provide a firmer foundation for recovery.”
The selloff follows sustained withdrawals from US spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs). BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) recorded more than $2 billion in net outflows across nine consecutive trading sessions through Wednesday, while broader funds shed nearly $1.44 billion over five sessions.
Preliminary Farside Investors data showed another $47.7 million in net outflows on Thursday, although figures for BlackRock and Fidelity were still pending.
Related: Bitcoin hovers near $74K as stocks rise despite US bond yield rebound

articles.title: Bitcoin Drops to $69K On 'Concentrated Liquidation' and 'Weakening' Demand - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Bitcoin slipped 5% on Friday, briefly dropping below $69,000. It is the lowest price the leading cryptocurrency has sit since August.
- Market analysts say the downward move was triggered by a "concentrated liquidation" and "weakening" demand for crypto across ETFs, stablecoins, and treasury firms.
- It also comes in the wake of a "hotter than expected" consumer price index report and Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigning from the company.
Leading cryptocurrency Bitcoin has dropped 5.6% on the day, and is currently trading at just over $69,300, per Decrypt data. It comes after the latest consumer price index, or CPI, results came in "hotter than expected," experts said, with the drop was triggered by a "concentrated liquidation."
Bitcoin's plunge took it to a 24-hour low of $67,922, its lowest level since mid-August, when it boosted from $63,000.
"Bitcoin’s drop below $69,000 was directly triggered by a concentrated liquidation of leveraged long positions," Tim Sun, senior analyst at Hashkey, told Decrypt. "Though the deeper issue lies in steadily weakening market demand."
Sun highlighted U.S. Bitcoin spot ETFs recording six consecutive days of net outflows, according to CoinGlass. He also pointed to stablecoin supply shrinking and MSCI removing digital asset treasury firm Strategy from its funds.
"ETFs, stablecoin liquidity, and corporate treasuries have served as the primary capital pillars supporting this Bitcoin rally," Sun said. "With all three coming under simultaneous pressure, the market is losing the marginal buying power that previously propelled prices higher."
Meanwhile, other major cryptocurrencies have also taken a hit. Ethereum has dropped 4.6% on the day to $1,953, BNB has slipped 4.7% to $639.46, and Solana is down 3.1% to $80.47, according to Decrypt data. The global crypto market cap has dropped 4.6% over the past 24 hours to $2.39 trillion.
It follows U.S. CPI rising 0.4% in October, which is "hotter than expected, even if the headline monthly rate eased to 0.4% from September’s 0.6%," according to CoinShares head of research James Butterfill. "More troubling was the composition," he added. "Food rose 0.5%, services remained firm, and core CPI increased 0.3%, with services excluding rent, a gauge of domestic price pressure the Fed watches closely, rising 0.5%. The inflation problem is therefore no longer easily dismissed as an oil story."
The consumer price index, or CPI, is a way of measuring inflation that tracks the average price changes of everyday goods and services over time. Central banks tend to use CPI to inform whether they'll cut or hike interest rates, meaning higher-than-expected CPI signals a potential Federal Reserve hike.
Polymarket predictors put a 97% chance on the Fed raising interest rates this year, up from 75% at the start of the week. The CME FedWatch tool, meanwhile, sees an 88% chance of a 25 basis point hike, with 12% anticipating a 50 basis point rise.
On top of the CPI, Bitcoin's downward move comes following Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned from the company, after reports of multiple affairs including with a suspected Chinese spy and a senior company executive spread.
Huang's departure has sparked "severe volatility across tech stocks, further dampening market risk appetite," Sun told Decrypt. "This has prompted broader portfolio de-risking, amplifying the downward pressure on Bitcoin," he added.
For a crypto rebound to happen, Sun said that Bitcoin needs "long-term allocation capital" to flow back into crypto after ETFs, stablecoins, and digital asset treasury companies have taken a hit in recent weeks.

articles.title: US courts target $1.2B in stolen Binance funds, yet victims face a new hurdle
articles.text:
Quick Take
- DOJ disclosed court authority to seize or restrain more than $1.2 billion stolen from Binance in its Nov. 12 announcement.
- The release leaves forfeiture completion and return timing unresolved.
- Binance's Nov. 3 promise to absorb the loss concerns company funding, separate from recovering the stolen assets.
US authorities have secured court authorization to seize or restrain more than $1.2 billion stolen from Binance funds, advancing the legal effort to recover assets from the October theft.
The Department of Justice (DOJ) disclosed the authorization on Nov. 12 but did not announce completed forfeiture or a timetable for returning the money.
The court-covered assets sit within more than $2.7 billion frozen through combined US government and private-sector efforts, according to the department.
The larger figure measures the combined freezing effort, while the smaller one identifies the portion for which DOJ reports seizure or restraint authority.
Binance had already committed to covering its losses in its Nov. 3 incident report. The exchange promised to absorb the financial impact of the stolen funds and said it had set aside more than 100% of what it would need to cover the loss.
DOJ attributes the theft of more than $6 billion on or about Oct. 29 to North Korean military actors known as TraderTraitor. Its announcement said efforts to trace, freeze, seize and forfeit the stolen assets remained ongoing as the attackers continued laundering them through cryptocurrency bridges, mixers and exchanges.
Court authority leaves further recovery steps for Binance funds
The department's detailed account uses the wording “seize or restrain” and does not break down how much of the covered pool falls into each category.
The authorization establishes the scope of court-backed action over part of the frozen assets, without establishing that the entire amount is already seized.
The release describes forfeiture efforts as ongoing, and leaves the eventual recipients and distribution route unspecified.
DOJ's general guidance on compensation from forfeited assets helps explain the distinction between securing assets and paying victims.
Before remission can occur, the government must identify, seize, and forfeit assets.
The court authorization marks progress in recovering the stolen haul. The Nov. 12 announcement leaves unanswered how much is ultimately forfeited, who receives the assets, and when any return occurs.

articles.title: Trump Picks Hester Peirce Successor at SEC
articles.text:
Trump nominates Hester Peirce successor among SEC, CFTC picks
The White House also named a former CFTC commissioner and two CLARITY Act veterans as nominees to fill vacancies at the SEC and CFTC.
US President Donald Trump has nominated Steven Levine to replace former Securities and Exchange Commission Commissioner Hester Peirce, one of the agency’s most prominent crypto advocates, as part of four nominations to fill vacancies at the SEC and Commodity Futures Trading Commission.
The White House’s latest announcement on Thursday named two nominees each for the SEC and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, agencies whose decisions help shape US cryptocurrency regulation, among other functions. All four nominations require Senate confirmation.
The nominations would replenish several commissioner roles. The SEC currently has only two of its five commissioner seats filled, while CFTC Chairman Michael Selig is the sole member of his agency’s five-seat commission.
The nominations come weeks before Democrats are set to take control of the Senate in January, giving a narrow window for Republicans to confirm Trump’s picks.
Related: House Finance panel chair says regulator actions on crypto ‘fall short’ of CLARITY bill
Levine, a Republican, was nominated for an SEC term ending June 5, 2030, replacing Peirce, who left the agency in October. Peirce was a leading advocate for clearer crypto rules at the SEC, helping shape its approach to digital assets as the former head of its Crypto Task Force, while Levine’s views on crypto regulation are less publicly established.
Trump also nominated Democrat Kristin Johnson, a former CFTC commissioner, for the SEC seat held by Caroline Crenshaw, whose term has also expired. Johnson’s proposed term ends June 5, 2029. Johnson has advocated for stronger customer protections and conflict-of-interest rules for crypto firms in her time at the CFTC.
For the CFTC, Trump nominated Republican Nathan Anonick and Democrat Matthew Rowland, both of whom worked on the Clarity Act. CFTC Chairman Mike Selig called them “two strong bipartisan picks” for CFTC commissioners and said he looked forward to working with them upon their confirmation.
The nominees would typically appear before the Senate Banking Committee for the SEC positions and the Senate Agriculture Committee for the CFTC roles. Following committee consideration, their nominations would go to the full Senate, where confirmation requires a majority vote.
Magazine: Can the SEC and CFTC’s pro-crypto rules be overturned? Legal opinion

articles.title: Congress Summons Ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, Lutnick Over Chip Exports to China - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Senate Banking Committee Chairman Tim Scott has asked former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick to testify in December, warning of subpoenas.
- The chairs of three House committees separately want Huang and Nvidia General Counsel Tim Teter to sit for closed-door interviews on December 1 and 2.
- The inquiries focus on export controls and Megaspeed, a Singapore-based Nvidia customer whose former executive U.S. officials suspect of spying for China.
Sen. Tim Scott (R-SC), chairman of the Senate Banking Committee, has asked former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick to testify, widening a congressional inquiry that has moved from Huang's private life to U.S. controls on chip exports to China. "The American people deserve answers," Scott wrote in a tweet announcing the requests on Thursday evening.
In a letter dated November 12, Scott asked Huang to appear voluntarily at a public hearing on December 3 over public reports that "raise significant national security concerns." The committee has jurisdiction over export controls, "including their application to NVIDIA's exports of advanced semiconductors," he wrote. If Huang does not appear, the committee "is prepared to use all tools at our disposal, including subpoenas."
Recent reports raise serious concerns about our national security and the protection of sensitive U.S. technology.
I am requesting that NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick testify before the Senate Banking Committee.
The American people deserve… pic.twitter.com/Xu1kiNzkhW
— Senator Tim Scott (@SenatorTimScott) November 13, 2026
Scott asked Lutnick to testify on December 10, noting Commerce's "central role in issuing and enforcing export control regulations." A Lutnick spokesperson told NBC News that he had "proactively agreed to appear voluntarily," while the White House said President Donald Trump "maintains complete confidence" in Lutnick.
Separately on Thursday, the Republican chairs of the House Foreign Affairs, China and Intelligence committees, Reps. Brian Mast (R-FL), John Moolenaar (R-MI) and Rick Crawford (R-AR), wrote to Huang, Nvidia General Counsel Tim Teter and Jeffrey Kessler, the Commerce Department's under secretary for industry and security.
Huang was asked to sit for a closed-door, transcribed interview on December 1 and Teter on December 2, with each given until 8 p.m. on Friday to agree or face a subpoena. Kessler, whose bureau administers export controls, was invited to a hearing on December 3.
"As reports continue to come to light regarding Jensen Huang, NVIDIA, and MegaSpeed, there are clear national security concerns that need to be addressed immediately," the three chairs said in a statement. They called on Congress to add four chip security bills to the annual defense authorization bill.
It is their second request. A letter dated November 4 had asked Huang to brief the committees on November 18. Mast told reporters on Thursday that Huang had agreed to brief lawmakers, NBC News reported.
Megaspeed and export controls
At the center of the inquiries is Megaspeed, a Singapore-based Nvidia customer. U.S. officials suspected the company of helping Chinese firms get around restrictions on advanced AI chips, The New York Times reported in October. Its sister company in Malaysia bought at least $4.8 billion of AI equipment containing Nvidia chips between June 2024 and February 2026, according to trade records cited by the Times.
Megaspeed told the Times it had hired outside counsel to conduct an internal investigation. Nvidia has said it complies with U.S. export laws, according to NBC News.
The Times reported that U.S. officials had concluded that Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed executive, was a Chinese intelligence asset. China has rejected that as a smear, and Attorney General Todd Blanche said on Thursday that the Justice Department had not reached a conclusion on whether she was a spy, according to BBC News.
Jensen Huang admitted on Sunday to being unfaithful to his wife and resigned on Thursday. Nvidia's board has said it has no reason to believe national security or company secrets were compromised.
Moolenaar told reporters that Huang had "been one of the strongest proponents for not having export controls," Roll Call reported. On Wednesday, Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-MA), the Banking Committee's ranking member, and Sen. Chris Coons (D-DE) asked Lutnick, Secretary of State Marco Rubio and White House Chief of Staff Stephen Miller to preserve records on Nvidia chip exports to China.
China's foreign ministry warned on Friday that tighter U.S. export controls on semiconductors would threaten the stability of global supply chains, Al Jazeera reported.
Nvidia shares closed down 4.3% at $166.19 on Thursday and were up 2.7% at $170.63 in premarket trading early on Friday, according to Yahoo! Finance. The company has lost almost $500 billion in market value since the close on Friday, November 6. It reports quarterly earnings on Tuesday, the first under interim CEO Colette Kress.

articles.title: Diesel prices plunge 8%, yet Bitcoin traders face a squeeze
articles.text:
Quick Take
- October’s PPI showed diesel falling 7.9% as truck freight rose 3.9%, keeping the wholesale inflation picture mixed.
- PPI excluding food, energy and trade services rose 0.5% again, limiting the evidence of broad wholesale disinflation.
- Broader inflation cooling and completed ETF inflows would strengthen Bitcoin’s recovery case; financing relief remains conditional.
US wholesale inflation slowed in October, but rising freight prices and firm underlying pressure complicate the case that cheaper fuel will make financing easier for Bitcoin (BTC) holders while BTC remains below $70,000.
The Bureau of Labor Statistics’ October producer-price report, released Nov. 13, showed diesel prices falling 7.9% as truck freight prices rose 3.9%. Headline wholesale inflation slowed sharply, but the measure excluding food, energy, and trade services kept rising at September’s monthly pace.
Final-demand PPI rose 0.3% in October, seasonally adjusted, after September’s revised 1.4% increase.
The measure excluding food, energy and trade services rose 0.5% for a second month. Its annual increase eased to 4.9% from 5%, while headline annual PPI accelerated to 6.5% from 6.3%. Those readings support a mixed assessment of some comparisons improved, but underlying monthly pressure held firm.
BLS attributed more than 80% of October’s 0.2% rise in final-demand services prices to truck freight. Transportation and warehousing services rose 2%, even as final-demand energy prices slipped 0.1%. Goods prices increased 0.5%.
Cheaper diesel coexisted with higher prices for moving goods. For now, the freight increase undercuts an assumption that a lower fuel bill immediately means cheaper transport.
Unprocessed intermediate goods prices fell 3.1%. Alongside slower monthly headline inflation and the easing annual exclusion measure, that gives the more optimistic interpretation real evidence. The question is whether that cooling broadens and lasts.
The hurdle for Bitcoin extends beyond PPI
PPI measures the selling prices domestic producers receive, CPI measures prices paid by consumers, while the Fed targets inflation measured by personal consumption expenditures (PCE).
The measures overlap in the economic pressures they describe, but their readings are not interchangeable.
Speaking before that day’s CPI release, Fed Governor Christopher Waller leaned toward further tightening through a 25-basis-point December rate increase if conditions developed as expected.
He said a 50-basis-point increase should be considered if October core CPI resembled the previous two readings around 0.3% or higher.
The subsequent CPI report showed a 0.4% monthly headline increase and a third consecutive 0.3% increase excluding food and energy.
The Fed’s explanation of monetary policy describes how policy-rate changes affect short-term interest rates and broader financial conditions. Applied to Bitcoin, the conditional mechanism is that lower financing costs could make borrowed exposure easier to carry, while easier conditions could encourage investors to allocate more to risk.
The route from producer prices to financing relief remains conditional. Persistent inflation could keep policy restrictive even when one fuel price falls, while a recovery case based on financing relief needs evidence beyond cheaper diesel.
Farside Investors' completed Nov. 12 row records US Bitcoin ETF net outflows of $284.1 million, preceding the PPI release.
ETF flows describe one investment channel. Still, completed inflows would provide firmer evidence of buyers returning than an inflation-based expectation alone.
Broader cooling in consumer and producer prices, less restrictive assessments from policymakers and observable financing relief would strengthen the case that fuel declines are becoming useful for Bitcoin holders.
Sustained ETF inflows would add demand evidence, while continued underlying inflation pressure and further withdrawals would keep that case weaker, even if diesel keeps getting cheaper.

articles.title: Jensen Huang Linked to Third Alleged Affair: Reuters
articles.text:
Former Nvidia CEO Huang had third alleged affair: Reuters
Reuters reported that Jensen Huang had a relationship with another Nvidia employee, hours after he resigned as CEO.
Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had an intimate relationship with a second company employee, Reuters reported, bringing the number of alleged extramarital affairs to three.
The report, citing two people familiar with the matter, followed Huang’s resignation as Nvidia CEO and a board member on Thursday. Reuters did not identify the other employee in its report and said attempts to reach her were unsuccessful.
The two previously reported relationships involved Alice Huang, whom US intelligence officials suspect of working for Chinese intelligence, and Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of health care.
Cointelegraph reached out to Nvidia for comment.
US Attorney General Todd Blanche said Thursday during a press conference that the Justice Department had not determined whether Alice Huang was a Chinese spy. He confirmed that the FBI was investigating reports that she worked for the Chinese government. Beijing has denied the allegations.
Nvidia shares fell more than 13% shortly after the US market opened on Thursday, trading at $151.00 as of 2:31 p.m. UTC, according to Yahoo Finance.
Venture capitalist Haseeb Qureshi argued that the mounting disclosures undermined Huang’s credibility, pushing back against tech industry figures defending the Nvidia co-founder.
“As others have said: ‘when you find two ants in your kitchen, the best estimate for the ants in your kitchen is not two,’” Qureshi wrote on X.
Related: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO, exits board; shares plunge

articles.title: XRP loans trigger 883 liquidations, and $53M remains at risk
articles.text:
Quick Take
- On Base, liquidators repaid 4 million USDC and seized 4.18 million cbXRP across 883 events from Nov. 7 through 13.
- A checked Nov. 10 transaction shows seized cbXRP moving onward on Base, while the native XRP selling link remains unproven.
- At the Nov. 13 snapshot, the market carried 53.5 million USDC of debt, keeping borrower collateral buffers important.
XRP-backed borrowers surrendered about 4.18 million cbXRP in 883 liquidation events on Morpho, as liquidators repaid just over 4 million USDC of debt.
The activity took place in a lending market on Base where borrowers pledge cbXRP to borrow USDC.
CryptoSlate's analysis of Morpho's indexed transaction records covers Nov. 7 at 10:30:51 UTC through Nov. 13 before 13:00 UTC. The 883 events count individual liquidation logs, so one person can be represented more than once.
A later snapshot on Nov. 13 still showed 53.53 million USDC outstanding.
An earlier loan-stress coverage used Nov. 6 positions to estimate that a further 10% oracle-price decline could bring 8.84 million USDC of debt across 1,070 positions to liquidation eligibility, assuming balances stayed unchanged.
What XRP borrowers gave up
The market's liquidation threshold is 62.5% loan-to-value, which compares the debt with the collateral's value: falling collateral prices can push the same loan above the permitted ratio.
Under Morpho's liquidation mechanism, an outside liquidator can repay some or all of an eligible position's debt and receive collateral plus an incentive. Here, that means paying USDC and taking cbXRP.
Collateral leaves the position while the debt obligation shrinks, and the records alone do not fully capture each borrower's economic outcome.
The largest daily repayment total in the selected window was about 1.58 million USDC on Nov. 8, followed by about 1.06 million on Nov. 10. All 883 selected liquidation records reported zero bad debt, the debt left uncovered by collateral.
The decoded liquidation log for a Nov. 10 transaction shows about 202,394 USDC repaid, and 218,175 cbXRP seized in the same market.
The liquidator then sent that cbXRP amount to another address and received USDC and wrapped ETH from that address in the same transaction. A separate Nov. 7 log records about 1,050 USDC repaid against 1,029 cbXRP seized.
Establishing native XRP selling would require evidence linking the seized collateral to subsequent XRP trading, including any redemption or custody movement along the way.
Substantial borrowing remains
At the API's 16:28:22 UTC state timestamp on Nov. 13, the Base market still carried approximately 53.5 million USDC of debt against 121.7 million cbXRP of collateral.
Coinbase's loan-health guidance says repaying debt or adding collateral can improve a position's health. Optional automatic collateral protection depends on available assets and can fail during volatility or technical problems.
The next consequences for remaining borrowers depend on their own collateral buffers, repayments, and top-ups. The next evidence for XRP holders assessing selling pressure is the destination and use of seized cbXRP, followed by any traceable redemption or native XRP trade.

articles.title: Gemini Retail Crypto Trading Hits 3-Year Low in Q3
articles.text:
Gemini’s quarterly retail trading volume sinks to 3-year low
Gemini’s third-quarter trading rebound masked a deepening retail slump.
Crypto exchange Gemini has just reported its lowest quarterly retail trading volume in three years, despite an increase in overall crypto trading volume.
Total spot trading volume rose 18% from the second quarter to $4.5 billion, according to Gemini’s Q3 earnings report. Institutional volume climbed 26% to $3.9 billion, while retail volume fell 14% to $600 million, its lowest level since the third quarter of 2023.
Gemini said the quarterly increase in spot trading volume was “supported by increased institutional Zcash activity and expanded affiliated market-making,” but did not give a specific reason for the decline in retail trading.
Despite the retail slump, Gemini’s exchange revenue increased 7% from the previous quarter to $13.4 million as institutional revenue more than doubled. Retail traders remained its largest source of exchange revenue, contributing nearly three-quarters of the total.
Crypto exchanges turn to prediction markets for growth
A number of crypto exchanges also reported softer crypto trading activity in the most recent quarter.
Coinbase reported softer retail and institutional activity, with consumer spot trading volume falling 9% from the previous quarter to $23.4 billion. Coinbase chief financial officer Alesia Haas said “continued growth in prediction markets helped offset softer crypto trading activity.”
At Robinhood, crypto revenue fell 55% year-on-year to $120 million, offset by a sixfold increase in event-contract revenue to $173 million.
Related: Strategy stock sheds 5% amid MSCI index removal, Bitcoin sell-off
Gemini also got some help from its own prediction exchange, Gemini Predictions, with revenue from that business unit increasing 52% quarter-on-quarter to $796,000, though it wasn’t significant enough to offset declines elsewhere.
Gemini looks to expand prediction markets
Gemini reported stronger prediction-market activity heading into the fourth quarter, with average daily traders in October running about 50% above the third-quarter average.
Nearly a third of new prediction traders were new to Gemini, more than double the proportion in Q3.
The company is also seeking to distribute its event contracts through other platforms. An August nonbinding agreement with Apex Fintech Solutions would make Gemini Titan the exclusive venue for crypto event contracts distributed through Apex’s futures brokerage to its brokerage customers, subject to definitive agreements.
Gemini is set to host a Q3 earnings call on Friday.

articles.title: FBI warns active $400M crypto scam targets your friends by replacing your face in videos
articles.text:
Quick Take
- The FBI seized over 900 victim webcam videos as authorities disrupted infrastructure used in North Korea's FaceStealer scheme.
- Stolen accounts and recorded faces lure contacts into fake meetings, where attackers use a supposed technical fix to install malware.
- The FBI recommends confirming invitations through another channel and refusing scripts or terminal code presented as video-client updates.
North Korean hackers are using stolen webcam recordings to impersonate crypto workers in fake meetings with their contacts, turning one victim's familiar face into bait for the next attack, the FBI warns.
The Justice Department announced disruption of cloud-based infrastructure used in FaceStealer on November 12. It said the scheme had caused more than $400 million in cryptocurrency theft over the preceding 18 months and that the FBI had seized over 900 victim webcam videos under a federal warrant.
The DOJ release treats FaceStealer separately from the Binance theft, which CryptoSlate has covered through the FBI's attribution and the exchange's asset-replenishment delays.
A familiar account opens the door
In its November 12 FLASH advisory, the FBI describes attackers taking over genuine accounts on services including Telegram, LinkedIn, Slack and Discord. Access to chat histories lets them tailor an invitation to earlier conversations, giving a new approach the context of an existing relationship.
A legitimate calendaring service can handle the scheduling. The malicious meeting link arrives shortly before the call, directing the target to a copycat Zoom or Microsoft Teams session controlled by the attackers.
Once the target enters, stored webcam footage makes it appear that the known contact has joined. Attackers can simulate several participants. The familiar person on screen can therefore be a real prior victim's recording, rather than a live participant.
The FBI says FaceStealer still overwhelmingly relies on stolen genuine videos. Generated deepfakes provide an additional way to impersonate participants.
The target's webcam becomes part of the attack before the supposed troubleshooting begins. The FLASH says recording starts when the target first clicks the imposter meeting link. The attackers can later use that footage to impersonate the target.
During the meeting, an attacker claims there is an audio or other technical problem. The proposed remedy can be an update prompt, a script or code to paste into a terminal. Following the instructions installs malware, which the FBI says can include tools for harvesting browser cookies, logging keystrokes, capturing screens and maintaining access to the device.
That is where the scheme joins theft to impersonation. Access to the computer can expose cryptocurrency or other valuable access. Stolen communication accounts, contact lists and webcam footage give the hackers material for the next approach. The FBI's FaceStealer resource page describes the same cycle of compromise, account hijacking and fake meetings.
The damage is not necessarily immediate. The FBI reported cases in which cryptocurrency theft and communication-account takeovers came months to more than a year after the initial compromise. A quiet period after a suspicious meeting therefore does not establish that a device or account is safe.
Check the invitation before trusting the face
The FBI recommends using the official meeting application with an invite code and, where possible, confirming an invitation through a different communication channel. That checks the approach beyond the account the attacker may already control.
It also advises delaying webcam activation until the inviter can be seen, heard and communicated with. An apparent technical fault should not lead to running scripts or pasting terminal code presented as a video-client update.
For people who suspect compromise, the bureau recommends securing cryptocurrency in a new crypto wallet created on an unaffected device, securing communication and developer accounts, alerting contacts and employers, and reporting to IC3 with the keyword FaceStealer. Alerting contacts can interrupt further approaches that could reuse the stolen account and recording.

articles.title: Aave plan could cut some lenders’ share of interest by 60%
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Aave’s proposed interest split would cut Polygon DAI lenders’ share from 75% to 30%, without directly changing the borrowing-rate curve.
- Polygon DAI faces a modeled 2.70 percentage point APY cut, while selected collateral reserves would lose minimal lending yield.
- Plasma USDT0’s modeled annual revenue contribution remains conditional on finalized terms, and supplier exits could alter the proposal’s fixed inputs.
Aave lenders supplying DAI on Polygon could see their share of borrower interest fall from 75% to 30% under a November 12 proposal by TokenLogic. The plan would redirect more interest to Aave’s DAO treasury, with uneven cuts to lender returns across its markets.
The November 12 proposal covers 54 reserves across 12 Aave V3 instances and Ethereum V2. TokenLogic estimates about $4 million in additional annualized DAO revenue using November 9 balances and rates. That total includes roughly $1 million from Plasma USDT0, a change that would enter the formal proposal only once its terms are finalized.
In Aave’s lending system, the mechanism is the reserve factor: the portion of borrower interest allocated to the DAO instead of suppliers. Raising it changes who receives the interest, without directly changing the borrowing-rate curve. TokenLogic argues the larger share would better compensate the DAO for the risks attached to borrowable reserves.
Polygon DAI lenders face a larger cut
Polygon V3 DAI illustrates how much that allocation can matter. TokenLogic proposes raising its reserve factor from 25% to 70%, with a modeled supply APY reduction of 270 basis points, or 2.70 percentage points. The same line projects $94,373 in additional annual DAO revenue.
With the amount of borrower interest unchanged, suppliers’ share would fall from 75% to 30%. The treasury would receive the difference. In that fixed-input model, the revenue gain comes from a smaller payment to lenders, without requiring more borrowing or a higher price for the same loan.
The comparison with other stablecoins shows that the proposal does not apply a uniform yield reduction. TokenLogic models cuts of 173 basis points for Avalanche DAI.e, 78 for Avalanche USDt and 61 for Avalanche USDC. Their proposed reserve factors are 90%, 25% and 25%, respectively.
For savers choosing where to lend stablecoins, those reductions change the return offered for keeping liquidity in the affected reserve. TokenLogic identifies Polygon DAI as a legacy reserve and explicitly uses lower returns as an incentive to move liquidity out of declining markets.
Modeled supply APY changes in TokenLogic’s November 12 proposal using November 9, 2026 balances and rates. Negative values are reductions; 100 basis points equals 1 percentage point. Selected reserves, not the complete proposal.
A separate Aavescan observation puts the Polygon DAI pool in perspective. Its November 12 midnight-UTC snapshot records 3.30 million DAI deposited, 2.65 million borrowed and a 4.81% supply APR, excluding historical incentives.
Aavescan’s observed APR and TokenLogic’s modeled APY reduction, based on November 9 inputs, describe different rate measures at different dates.
The largest reserve-factor percentages do not necessarily impose the largest yield cuts. TokenLogic proposes 100% factors for selected bitcoin-wrapper and liquid-staking collateral reserves whose lending APYs are already close to zero. Its model puts the lost lending yield in that group at no more than 1 to 2 basis points.
A 100% reserve factor applies to lending interest, not deposit principal. For wstETH, it is also separate from the staking accrual reflected in the token’s stETH value. Redirecting Aave’s incremental lending interest would leave that underlying accrual mechanism intact.
The revenue estimate holds balances and rates fixed
Plasma USDT0 shows why a modest yield cut can still produce a large revenue estimate. TokenLogic models a reserve-factor increase from 5% to 7.5% against about $632 million borrowed. The projected supply APY reduction is 16 basis points, alongside about $1 million in additional annual revenue. Its inclusion remains conditional on finalized Plasma terms.
Even for the other lines, annualizing November 9 balances and rates holds the inputs fixed. The proposal also seeks to change supplier behavior, which could alter those inputs.
For Ethereum V2, TokenLogic proposes raising five remaining borrowed reserves to 99.99%, directing nearly all their interest to the DAO. It expects reduced returns to encourage exits. If suppliers withdraw, utilization could rise and borrowing costs could increase, creating pressure on borrowers to close positions.
Aave’s utilization-based borrowing curve links borrowing costs to how much liquidity is in use. That potential response is separate from changing the curve itself, as in the USDT borrowing-rule update CryptoSlate covered in October.
The November 12 publication lists feedback and escalation to the Aave Improvement Proposal stage as next steps. Its yield cuts and revenue gains remain proposed estimates.

articles.title: Amazon says no human wrote or reviewed the code for its new cloud testing tool
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Amazon released AWS Emulator on November 11, saying autonomous agents wrote and reviewed its implementation.
- Human engineers built the guardrails and release checks, while fidelity tests measure specific behavior against real AWS.
- Uncovered behavior remains unverified, and AWS requires testing application security on the real cloud before production.
Amazon released AWS Emulator on Nov. 11, a local tool that imitates AWS services so developers can test cloud applications on their own machines. The company says autonomous AI agents wrote and reviewed its implementation.
In Amazon's engineering account, engineer Matthew Goldberg says his team neither wrote nor reviewed the emulator code. He also describes the substantial engineering work needed to turn an experiment into a product, including the guardrails and checks that determine which changes can ship.
Amazon describes three teams of agents: one manages fidelity tests, another finds differences between the emulator and real AWS, and a third fixes individual issues. Changes face checks for compilation, coding standards, security and regressions before merging, according to the company.
The test agents work from public AWS API models and verify their scenarios against the real cloud. The public evaluation suite says every fidelity test was checked against at least two sandboxed AWS accounts.
What a passing test establishes
AWS calls the degree of agreement with its cloud services “fidelity.” A test passes when the emulator matches AWS for every call in that workflow, including status codes, resulting resources, side effects and errors, according to its fidelity documentation. Returning success where AWS returns an error fails that test.
The boundary is coverage. The evaluation repository explicitly says behavior without a fidelity test is unverified. Passing a scenario establishes a match for that scenario; it does not establish that every way an application uses AWS will work.
Security has a separate limit. AWS's security guidance warns against using the emulator to determine whether an application is secure. It does not check AWS KMS key policies or Amazon S3 bucket policies, and a request denied by AWS may succeed locally.
Agent review of implementation security therefore cannot be read as validation of a user's application permissions. The emulator is for building and testing, not production workloads. AWS instructs developers to test their whole application and security settings on real AWS before production.
For builders adopting agent-written software, the release makes the acceptance process as relevant as the code's authorship: which behaviors are checked, what remains outside coverage, and where the developer must still test against the real service.

articles.title: Lido Earn’s new safety net still leaves depositors on the hook for losses
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Lido Earn added Firelight protection on November 5, with eligible approved losses absorbed before the separate DAO share buffer.
- Lido’s dated illustration implies combined cushions near 7.2% for EarnETH and 12.1% for EarnUSD, subject to each layer’s conditions.
- Current Meta Treasury pays Firelight premiums separately, while exclusions, approval requirements and finite capital can leave losses with depositors.
Lido Earn’s DeFi vaults gained a new layer of loss protection on Nov. 5, 2026, with different potential cushions for ETH and dollar depositors. Lido’s published illustration puts combined protection near 7.2% of EarnETH assets and 12.1% of EarnUSD assets, subject to eligibility, approval and available capital.
Firelight, an onchain protection protocol, now absorbs eligible approved losses before the existing Lido DAO buffer. Each layer has its own conditions and capital limits.
Lido Earn’s vaults put deposits into DeFi strategies. EarnETH allocates ETH and stETH, while EarnUSD offers dollar-denominated strategies. Users receive tokens representing their vault shares, whose value reflects performance. Protection attaches specifically to Earn vault deposits, with stETH used as an input to EarnETH’s strategies.
Lido Earn protection limits and qualifying losses
For the first 30-day period beginning Nov. 5, Lido says Firelight can absorb eligible, approved losses up to 5.7% of EarnETH’s total value locked, or TVL, and 8% of EarnUSD’s, within limits for each protected market.
Its November illustration puts EarnETH’s assets at $212.9 million, with up to $12.1 million from Firelight and $3.2 million from the DAO position. Lido states a combined ceiling of $15.4 million. For EarnUSD, it lists $50.3 million in assets, up to $4 million from Firelight and $2.1 million from the DAO, totaling $6.1 million.
Dividing Lido’s stated combined totals by those vault assets gives approximately 7.2% for EarnETH and 12.1% for EarnUSD. Its rounded ETH components add to $15.3 million rather than $15.4 million; both produce 7.2% to one decimal place.
This snapshot combines Nov. 5 vault sizes and first-period Firelight limits with DAO positions referenced to its Sept. 30 quarterly reporting. The dollar estimates come from Lido’s November illustration and should not be treated as Nov. 13 balances.
The totals also assume Firelight can fund a payout in full. Lido says settlement capital may leave payment below the validated loss. A larger illustrated percentage therefore does not, by itself, establish that EarnUSD has lower overall investment risk.
Firelight’s integration announcement identifies six failure categories: smart contract exploits, oracle failures, governance exploits, and bad debt, depegs or redemption failures caused by a protocol mechanism failing. A falling asset price or a depeg alone does not establish eligibility.
Lido says ordinary price moves and liquidations using accurate prices are excluded, alongside stolen keys, user error, offchain issues and flaws known before a protection period began. Protected markets and limits remain fixed for each 30-day period. Capital moved into a new market midway through a period becomes protected only when a later period includes it.
An independent consortium of five security and risk firms must approve Firelight’s loss assessment. Approved payments draw first on its reserve, then on staked capital.
Lido said on Nov. 5 that Current Meta Treasury pays for this protection, so the premium does not come out of vault returns. That funding is separate from the DAO’s invested loss-absorbing position.
The DAO buffer can still leave losses with users
The DAO layer operates under its own mandate and is not restricted to specific causes. Once a loss of at least 1% of a vault’s TVL is confirmed, the Growth Committee can burn up to all DAO-held shares in that affected vault. The mandate can be changed by DAO vote.
Lido’s original DAO mechanism was backed by an allocation of $3 million worth of wstETH to EarnETH and $2 million in USDC to EarnUSD. Those deposits hold shares on ordinary depositor terms, earning returns and carrying risk. Burning them reduces the share supply to offset losses for other holders. The capital available through this mechanism is limited to the DAO’s vault position.
Both layers operate at vault level, so depositors do not need to submit individual compensation requests. Incident approval, the DAO’s activation threshold and each layer’s capital limits still apply. Lido also says neither layer is insurance or a guarantee, and that Firelight protection gives depositors no right of action against a Firelight party.
A loss outside Firelight’s scope may still qualify under the DAO’s separate mandate. Any loss left after applicable protection, including amounts above market limits or beyond available capital and DAO shares, can remain with depositors.

articles.title: New US report reveals yen rescue used euros, not dollars. That matters for Bitcoin
articles.text:
Quick Take
- The November 12 report confirms Treasury bought yen with ESF euros in July, separating currency support from dollar funding.
- Central-bank dollar swaps outstanding fell from $250 million in June to $207 million in September; BOJ had none at quarter-end.
- Yen appreciation and margin pressure could force leveraged investors to cut risk, but current Bitcoin flows remain unestablished.
The US Treasury financed July’s yen intervention with euros from its reserves, the New York Fed confirmed in a November 12 report. For Bitcoin, the funding currency limits the operation’s significance as a signal of fresh Federal Reserve dollar liquidity.
On July 31, the New York Fed bought 79.4 billion yen in the spot market against euro sales from Treasury’s Exchange Stabilization Fund, or ESF. The aim was to counter what Treasury viewed as disorderly yen moves.
The New York Fed executed the trade as Treasury’s fiscal agent. The Federal Reserve itself did not intervene in foreign-exchange markets during the third quarter. Treasury’s ESF operating framework identifies yen and euros as its foreign-currency assets and describes the New York Fed’s trading role. An exchange of those reserve currencies alone supplies no evidence of new Fed dollars entering Bitcoin markets.
A separate mechanism does provide dollar funding abroad: central-bank dollar liquidity swaps. Under those arrangements, the Fed exchanges dollars for a foreign central bank’s currency, with an agreement to reverse the transaction.
The report shows less borrowing outstanding through that facility at quarter-end. Aggregate balances fell from $250 million on June 30 to $207 million on September 30, 2026. The Bank of Japan had none outstanding at September’s end; the remaining balances were with the European Central Bank and Bank of England.
Offshore dollar funding conditions were stable during Q3, the report says, with generally low borrowing premiums in major currency pairs. Those quarter-end stocks do not measure gross lending during the quarter or establish November’s funding conditions.
Yen borrowing still carries risk
The more recent BOJ exchange-rate sheet recorded dollar/yen at 159.70–71 at 17:00 JST on November 12. That is a dated market observation, not an announced intervention threshold.
Bitcoin’s potential exposure runs through leverage. A stronger yen makes unhedged yen borrowing more expensive to repay in another currency. If volatility raises margin demands, leveraged investors may need to raise cash or cut positions, spreading pressure beyond the original currency trade.
Research by the Bank for International Settlements found that leveraged equity and currency unwinds amplified August 2024’s market shock, with margin increases and further reductions in leverage worsening volatility. Crypto also responds to wider financial conditions: IMF working-paper authors found that US monetary tightening reduced a broad crypto price factor through investors’ appetite for risk.
These mechanisms explain how a yen-funded unwind could pressure Bitcoin, but the report does not establish current Bitcoin flows or a present unwind. July’s euro-funded yen intervention is not evidence of new Fed dollars entering crypto.

articles.title: The cost of a $70,000 Bitcoin hedge more than doubled in a day
articles.text:
Quick Take
- The November 27 $70,000 put rose 127.6% between two BTC-denominated trades, while its reported implied volatility fell.
- The later ask was about $2,319.74 per one-BTC contract before fees, separate from the historical trade-price comparison.
- DVOL covers 30 days, versus roughly 14 for the put, so the index alone cannot establish inexpensive protection.
A Bitcoin hedge using a put with a $70,000 strike more than doubled in BTC terms between November 12 and 13, even as its reported implied volatility fell. On November 13, Deribit's broad volatility gauge hovered near 40, showing why a calm index alone cannot reveal the cost of protecting a holding.
Deribit observations from November 12–13 show its November 27 $70,000 put traded at 0.0145 BTC at 11:51 UTC on November 12 and 0.033 BTC at 10:15 UTC on November 13, an increase of 127.6% in BTC terms. Yet the implied volatility reported for those executions fell from 38.97% to 37.67%.
Bitcoin's index price at the two trades fell from $72,805.71 to $69,320.08, taking it from above the fixed strike to below it. A put provides protection against a fall below that strike at expiry. As Bitcoin falls, that fixed protection can become more valuable even without higher implied volatility.
For a new buyer at 10:40:51 UTC on November 13, the contract's order book showed a 0.0325 BTC bid and a 0.0335 BTC ask. With the index at $69,245.85, that ask equaled about $2,319.74 for one contract before fees. The 127.6% increase compares executed BTC prices, rather than measuring a change in executable asks.
A fixed strike changes the Bitcoin hedge bill
A protective put's premium is the price of protection at a specified strike and expiry. Implied volatility is one component of that price. The underlying price, the strike, the forward price and the time remaining also matter. CryptoSlate’s crypto options platform comparison explains how contract design, settlement and execution costs differ across venues.
The two executions do not isolate how much of the premium change came from each pricing input. The contract also had less time remaining at the second trade.
The currency of the quote adds another difference. Deribit's inverse Bitcoin options are priced in BTC, and one contract represents one BTC. Converting each selected trade at its own contemporaneous index gives about $1,055.68 on November 12 and $2,287.56 on November 13. The increase in those dollar equivalents was 116.7%, smaller than the BTC-denominated increase.
The $70,000 strike also does not promise a $70,000 net sale price. The buyer pays the BTC premium upfront, and trading fees, delivery fees, currency conversion and the settlement reference affect the net result. At expiry, an in-the-money inverse put settles through an immediately settling inverse futures contract into BTC, with the economic result of cash settlement. An out-of-the-money put expires worthless.
Deribit defines DVOL as forward-looking, annualized implied volatility over 30 days, assembled across strikes and expiries. The November 27 put had roughly 14 days remaining. One broad index and one shorter-dated contract therefore describe different exposures.
The completed November 13 hourly buckets from 00:00 through 09:00 UTC recorded intrahour lows and highs spanning 39.03 to 41.58. The 09:00 bucket closed at 39.93; the 10:00 bucket was still incomplete when captured at 10:40 UTC.
A November 13 analysis by The Daily Digits on CryptoQuant supplies historical context. It reports DVOL of 40.77 against a median of 77.8 across 290 daily closes since March 2021 when Bitcoin was at least 17.4% below its rolling 30-day closing high. Its median for qualifying 2026 observations was 49.9, a closer current-year benchmark.
Those daily observations can overlap within a single selloff. They are not 290 independent crises, and the study does not give an exact intraday timestamp tying its reading to the put quotes. The comparison establishes the study's historical framing, rather than a fair price for this hedge.
The observations preceded the PPI release window
October's Producer Price Index was scheduled for November 13 at 08:30 Eastern, or 13:30 UTC, after these market observations. The scheduled inflation release provides a clear checkpoint for observing any repricing; it does not establish a cause for the earlier move.
A useful before-and-after comparison would track the same contract's bid, ask and implied volatility alongside its forward price and time remaining, then examine pricing across strikes. That separates a change in the cost of buying protection from a change in volatility pricing more clearly than DVOL alone.
For a holder, the immediate consequence is already visible: maintaining a Bitcoin hedge at a fixed dollar strike can become more expensive as Bitcoin falls, even while the broad volatility gauge remains subdued.

articles.title: Bitcoin’s futures pile has a problem: less cash to fuel a rebound
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Bitcoin futures open interest hit 704,000 BTC, the highest since Sept. 24, as spot liquidity thinned.
- The 10-year Treasury auction saw the sharpest drop in bid-to-cover, from 2.77 to 2.46.
- Bitcoin tested the $68,000-$72,500 bid zone as US spot ETFs logged $1.9 billion in net outflows over eight sessions.
DWF Labs' Martin Lee noted that Bitcoin futures open interest stood at 704,000 BTC this week, the highest since Sept. 24, while spot market liquidity continued to thin.
Meanwhile, the Treasury's $25 billion 30-year bond auction on Nov. 12 drew a 2.36 bid-to-cover ratio, down from 2.54 in October, and cleared at 5.441% against a 5.437% when-issued yield, a 0.4-basis-point tail.
The 10-year sale two days earlier showed a sharper slide, with bid-to-cover at 2.46 against 2.77 in October.
The 10-year cleared at 5.02%, with indirect bidders taking about 61.2% of competitive awards versus 80.3% in October, and dealers taking 9.8% versus 2.5%. The 3-year sale on Nov. 9 drew 2.53 against 2.62.
The 30-year result sits within the range of recent sales, since August's new issue drew 2.39. The Treasury said on Nov. 4 that demand for short-term bills remained strong, so the auctions show weaker appetite for duration, and a retreat from US debt would be a larger claim.
Treasury expects $618 billion of privately held net borrowing in October through December and $800 billion in January through March. The $125 billion in 3-, 10-, and 30-year refunding sales raises about $28 billion in new cash.
Two-year yields near 4.835% and 10-year yields near 5.068% on Nov. 12 make cash and government debt more competitive with Bitcoin.
The 10-year fell 0.31, compared with 0.18 for the 30-year and 0.09 for the 3-year. October’s 10- and 30-year sales reopened existing securities, while November’s sales were new issues.
Two sources of liquidity for Bitcoin
Lee describes dollar-debasement demand and broader risk-on flows as two supports for Bitcoin in past rallies. Both helped in the 2020 to 2022 cycle, and in August the debasement narrative let Bitcoin hold up while AI stocks corrected.
He shared in a note:
“The limitation is that debasement alone rarely sustains a rally when the broader market is risk-off.”
He sees little chance of liquidity rotating into crypto until uncertainty from the midterms and a near-certain December hike clears. Adoption continues, with Airwallex launching its own chain and the NYSE advancing a tokenized stock platform.
Lee said Bitcoin options open interest recovered to 447,000 BTC from a dip between Nov. 6 and Nov. 9, though it remains 5% to 10% below October. Bitcoin's futures open interest is about 12% below its 2026 high, while Ethereum's is down about 30% since May and Solana's about 23% since June.
At an illustrative $72,000, 704,000 BTC equals about $51 billion of gross notional. Open interest counts outstanding contracts with a buyer and a seller on each, so it mixes long bets, short bets and hedges, and it describes positioning, a measure separate from fresh capital.
Glassnode noted on Nov. 11 that open interest had rebuilt toward September levels while Bitcoin sat about 15% below its September high, a pattern consistent with traders adding shorts during the decline.
Futures can amplify a rebound through short covering or a decline through forced closures, and both routes depend on spot liquidity.
The spot evidence
Glassnode’s Nov. 11 analysis found resting bids within 5% of price outweighing asks on Binance and Coinbase since Nov. 5, with the largest concentration between $68,000 and $72,500.
Wallets holding 100 to 1,000 BTC and 1,000 to 10,000 BTC are accumulating, and other cohorts are distributing. A resting bid shows willingness to buy, and whether purchases follow depends on the bid surviving, since bids can be pulled or overwhelmed.
Bitcoin fell below $72,000 on Nov. 12 with an intraday low near $71,255, entering the top of that band.
About 35% of short-term holder supply is in profit, and Bitcoin trades below the $75,600 short-term holder cost basis. CryptoQuant reported profitable supply falling from more than 15 million BTC to about 11 million.
The 30-day average Coinbase premium is negative, with the deepest discount since February. Stablecoin supply contracted $14 billion in 30 days, the fastest since June 2022.
Farside Investors showed about $2 billion of US spot ETF outflows from Nov. 2 through Nov. 11, including $300 million on Nov. 11.
Daily net flows across the US spot Bitcoin ETFs , showing seven of eight sessions with net outflows.
Where Bitcoin could go from here
Lee argued:
“We've seen outflows accelerate at the bottoms and inflows accelerate at the tops.”
DWF Labs' Oct. 22 study of 694 trading days found ETF flows correlated 0.54 with Bitcoin's prior five-day return and 0.03 with its next five-day return. Flows turned negative on the low day in seven of eight qualifying selloffs and positive on the peak day in seven of eight tops.
About 20% of ETF buying was historically tied to CME short hedges.
Glassnode puts the True Market Mean near $77,500, a modeled six-month liquidation concentration at $59,500 to $62,600, a June low near $58,500 and a short-liquidation cluster near $87,500.
A recovery would have stronger backing if buyers absorb selling in the $68,000 to $72,500 band, Bitcoin reclaims $75,600 and $77,500, the Coinbase premium turns positive and stablecoin supply resumes growing. That combination could make futures positioning fuel for a rebound.
If bids give way while holder profitability erodes and stablecoin supply keeps contracting, leveraged positions could amplify a decline. Glassnode’s modeled $59,500 to $62,600 zone marks a possible area of liquidation pressure, not a price target.

articles.title: Chính phủ Hà Lan nguy cơ tan rã, Thủ tướng họp khẩn cứu liên minh
articles.text:
TPO - Thủ tướng Hà Lan Rob Jetten vừa tổ chức cuộc họp khủng hoảng trong nhiều giờ với lãnh đạo cấp cao của 2 đảng đối tác thuộc liên minh cầm quyền, nhằm ngăn chặn nguy cơ chính phủ tan rã.
Thủ tướng Hà Lan Rob Jetten. (Ảnh: AP)
Nhiệm kỳ 4 năm của chính phủ liên minh gồm 3 đảng mới trải qua chưa đầy 9 tháng.
Cuối ngày 13/11, ông Jetten cho biết các đối tác trong liên minh đã nhất trí tiếp tục trao đổi trong những ngày tới, nhằm tìm cách cứu vãn chính phủ, sau cuộc tranh luận căng thẳng về kế hoạch thuế.
"Thời gian gần đây đã có những điều tích cực, nhưng cũng có những vấn đề chưa được giải quyết tốt, và điều đó ảnh hưởng đến mối quan hệ giữa chúng ta. Tình hình này có thể và cần phải được cải thiện, cả về nội dung chính sách, phương diện chính trị lẫn quan hệ cá nhân. Điều này đòi hỏi những cuộc thảo luận mang tính căn bản, và chúng tôi đã bắt đầu tiến hành từ hôm nay", ông nói.
Tuy nhiên, dấu hiệu căng thẳng trong liên minh tiếp tục bộc lộ khi chỉ vài phút sau đó.
Bà Dilan Yeşilgöz-Zegerius, lãnh đạo đảng Nhân dân vì tự do và dân chủ (VVD) cánh hữu, tuyên bố: "Theo quan điểm của chúng tôi, thử nghiệm về một chính phủ thiểu số đã thất bại. Không thể tiếp tục theo cách này. Cần có những điều chỉnh, và về nguyên tắc, những điều chỉnh như vậy hoàn toàn có thể thực hiện được".
Đây là cuộc khủng hoảng mới nhất trong bối cảnh chính trường Hà Lan bị chia rẽ sâu sắc. Trong 1 thập kỷ qua, nước này đã trải qua 4 cuộc tổng tuyển cử, khiến niềm tin của công chúng đối với các nhà lập pháp ngày càng suy giảm.
Ông Jetten - thủ tướng trẻ nhất trong lịch sử Hà Lan, nhậm chức với cam kết mở ra kỷ nguyên đồng thuận mới giữa các đảng phái trong Quốc hội. Tuy nhiên, cho đến nay, ông vẫn gặp khó khăn với việc xử lý những cuộc đấu đá chính trị giữa các đảng trong cơ quan lập pháp, thậm chí ngay trong chính liên minh cầm quyền của mình.
Trong tuần này, sự đoàn kết vốn đã mong manh trong nội các của ông Jetten tiếp tục bị suy giảm, khi các nghị sĩ thuộc đảng D66 trung dung của ông và đảng Dân chủ Cơ đốc giáo (CDA) trung hữu chấp thuận những sửa đổi do 2 đảng đối lập trung tả PRO và Volt đề xuất.
Động thái này nhằm thông qua gói thuế tại Quốc hội Hà Lan, trong cuộc bỏ phiếu sít sao vào tối 12/11.
Tuy nhiên, các điều khoản trong thỏa thuận khiến đảng VVD vô cùng tức giận. Ông Jesse Klaver - lãnh đạo đảng PRO, gọi thỏa thuận là "thuế với giới triệu phú".
Các nghị sĩ VVD bỏ phiếu phản đối kế hoạch. Ông Ruben Brekelmans - lãnh đạo nhóm nghị sĩ của đảng này tại Quốc hội nói với báo chí rằng cách hành xử của các đối tác trong liên minh là điều "đáng lo ngại".
"Tôi không ngờ CDA và D66 lại có thể chuyển hướng mạnh mẽ đến như vậy. Điều đó gây bất lợi cho nền kinh tế, cho hoạt động kinh doanh tại Hà Lan và cho đất nước chúng ta", ông nói.
TPO - Ukraine vừa phóng gần 1.200 máy bay không người lái (UAV) nhằm vào các mục tiêu của Nga trong đêm, đánh dấu một trong những cuộc tấn công đường không quy mô lớn nhất của nước này kể từ khi cuộc xung đột giữa hai nước nổ ra cách đây gần 5 năm.
