articles.title: ChatGPT Wallet lets OpenAI’s Dots agents make purchases for you
articles.text:
After launching its Dots AI agents platform earlier this year, OpenAI is launching a wallet for the agents. ChatGPT Wallet is rolling out starting today for ChatGPT Pro subscribers in the US aged 18 and older using a US billing address and “eligible US-issued American Express, Chase, Mastercard and Visa cards.”
ChatGPT Wallet lets OpenAI’s Dots agents make purchases for you
OpenAI says ChatGPT Wallet won’t share your actual credit card info with its AI agents.
After adding a card to the wallet, your Dots agents can use it to buy things in response to your prompts, but they’ll check in with you each time before checking out. OpenAI’s support page says every purchase with ChatGPT Wallet requires a security check with biometric verification like Face ID or a fingerprint scan.
After you review the AI agent’s purchase and sign off on it, OpenAI says that, similar to using tap to pay, Apple Pay, or Google Wallet, it substitutes your credit card details with a payment token, so your actual card info isn’t shared with your Dots agent or the business you’re buying from. Eventually, OpenAI says it expects “users to be able to delegate purchases entirely to their agent by setting clear parameters—such as spending limits, purchase categories, or time periods—and pre-approve those purchases.”
ChatGPT Wallet might not work everywhere. Some retailers have restrictions on AI agents or block them altogether. Earlier this year, Amazon blocked Meta’s Muse agents. OpenAI says that in order for agents to use ChatGPT Wallet, “websites need to ensure agents are not inadvertently blocked, and payment and risk systems need to recognize legitimate purchases made by agents.”

articles.title: Giảm lãi suất: Để người vay được lợi, người gửi tiền không thiệt
articles.text:
Hài hòa lợi ích người gửi tiền và người vay vốn
Yêu cầu giảm lãi suất đối với các tổ chức tín dụng (TCTD) do Ngân hàng Nhà nước (NHNN) đưa ra ngày 18/10 được kỳ vọng góp phần hạ chi phí vốn, hỗ trợ doanh nghiệp và thúc đẩy tăng trưởng kinh tế. Tuy nhiên, việc giảm lãi suất cần được thực hiện trên cơ sở hài hòa lợi ích giữa người gửi tiền, người vay vốn, đồng thời bảo đảm an toàn cho hệ thống ngân hàng.
Theo Phó Thống đốc NHNN Phạm Thanh Hà, đây là yêu cầu quan trọng để duy trì mặt bằng lãi suất thấp một cách bền vững, tránh tạo thêm áp lực đối với thanh khoản và an toàn hoạt động của các TCTD.
Đến thời điểm hiện tại, gần 30 ngân hàng thương mại đã công bố giảm lãi suất cho vay, với mức giảm phổ biến từ 1,5-2%/năm.
Theo ông Lê Ngọc Lâm, Chủ tịch HĐQT BIDV, ngân hàng thậm chí còn giảm lãi suất nhiều hơn so với mức 1,5-2 điểm phần trăm như NHNN yêu cầu. Qua đó, lãi suất cho vay sau khi điều chỉnh chỉ còn 6-7%/năm dành cho doanh nghiệp thuộc lĩnh vực sản xuất, kinh doanh và lĩnh vực ưu tiên.
Số liệu từ NHNN cho thấy, đến ngày 26/10/2026, dư nợ tín dụng toàn hệ thống đạt 20,8 triệu tỷ đồng, tăng 11,94% so với cuối năm 2025. Dòng vốn tín dụng tiếp tục tập trung vào lĩnh vực sản xuất, kinh doanh, các lĩnh vực ưu tiên và những động lực tăng trưởng quan trọng của nền kinh tế.
Mặc dù đà tăng của mặt bằng lãi suất đã chậm lại, Phó Thống đốc Phạm Thanh Hà cho rằng áp lực về chi phí vốn vẫn lớn, đòi hỏi các giải pháp điều hành phải tiếp tục được triển khai đồng bộ trong thời gian tới.
“Việc tiếp tục giảm mặt bằng lãi suất cần có sự vào cuộc đồng bộ, quyết liệt của các TCTD, trên cơ sở cân đối nguồn vốn, chi phí hoạt động và khả năng tài chính của từng ngân hàng”, Phó Thống đốc nói.
Về phía doanh nghiệp, trao đổi với VietNamNet, ông Nguyễn Quang Huân, Phó Chủ tịch Hội Doanh nhân tư nhân Việt Nam, Chủ tịch HĐQT Công ty cổ phần Halcom Việt Nam, nhìn nhận, yêu cầu giảm lãi suất là chủ trương rất kịp thời và cần thiết của NHNN trong bối cảnh chi phí vay vốn tăng cao, nhiều doanh nghiệp nhỏ và vừa gặp khó khăn khi tiếp cận vốn vay.
Khi lãi suất giảm, doanh nghiệp có thêm điều kiện để duy trì hoạt động, bổ sung vốn cho sản xuất; người dân có thêm động lực chi tiêu; qua đó góp phần thúc đẩy tổng cầu, tăng trưởng kinh tế.
Ông Huân cho rằng lãi suất ngân hàng phản ánh quy luật cung cầu của thị trường, nhưng thị trường cần phải được định hướng bằng các chính sách, thay vì dùng mệnh lệnh hành chính. Như vậy, việc giảm lãi suất mới bền vững trong dài hạn.
“Lãi suất giảm một cách thực chất, bền vững phải ở sự điều hành của nền kinh tế vĩ mô, trong khi kinh tế vĩ mô chịu tác động nhiều chiều. Chẳng hạn khi người dân, doanh nghiệp có đủ niềm tin, họ sẽ mang tiền đi đầu tư. Nếu không, nền kinh tế thiếu nguồn cung tiền, từ đó dẫn đến lãi suất tiền gửi tăng và kéo theo lãi suất cho vay tăng”, ông Huân dẫn chứng.
Theo ông, việc phải vay vốn với lãi suất cao khiến doanh nghiệp vừa và nhỏ không thể lớn, không thể cạnh tranh. Do vậy, khi lãi suất giảm, việc tiếp cận nguồn vốn giá rẻ sẽ giúp doanh nghiệp mạnh dạn đầu tư.
Ông Huân nêu thực trạng biên độ lợi nhuận của các doanh nghiệp sản xuất, xuất khẩu hiện khá thấp, khiến khả năng chấp nhận lãi suất vay cao bị hạn chế. Trong khi đó, một số doanh nghiệp bất động sản có thể chấp nhận mức lãi suất lên tới 20%/năm.
“Nếu đã có doanh nghiệp sẵn sàng vay vốn với mức lãi suất 20%/năm thì ngân hàng đương nhiên sẽ ưu tiên phân bổ, trong khi doanh nghiệp sản xuất khó có thể đáp ứng mức lãi suất tương tự. Vì vậy, cần có công cụ mang tính tổng thể để giảm lãi suất, bên cạnh những giải pháp về tỷ giá và ổn định kinh tế vĩ mô”, ông nói.
Từ thực tế hoạt động doanh nghiệp, Chủ tịch HĐQT Halcom Việt Nam cho biết, năm 2025, doanh nghiệp vay vốn ngân hàng với lãi suất khoảng 7%/năm, nhưng sang năm 2026 mức này lần lượt được điều chỉnh lên 8%, rồi 9%/năm. Theo ông, đây vẫn là mức có thể chấp nhận được so với biên lợi nhuận của doanh nghiệp hoạt động trong lĩnh vực năng lượng và cấp, thoát nước.
Tuy nhiên, về giảm lãi suất, đến nay ông nói "mới chủ yếu tiếp cận thông tin qua báo chí".
“Bản thân tôi đã trực tiếp hỏi một số ngân hàng về việc doanh nghiệp sản xuất năng lượng sạch như chúng tôi có được hỗ trợ lãi suất 2%/năm hay không, nhưng đến nay các ngân hàng này chưa có thông tin lại”, ông Huân cho hay.
Cần giải pháp đồng bộ để giảm lãi suất
Để đạt được mục tiêu giảm lãi suất lâu dài, TS. Nguyễn Văn Lộc - Giám đốc Chương trình đào tạo Kinh doanh thương mại, Đại học Phenikaa - cho rằng kiểm soát rủi ro tín dụng bất động sản và duy trì ổn định kinh tế vĩ mô là những điều kiện quan trọng để tạo dư địa giảm lãi suất, giảm phụ thuộc vào tín dụng ngân hàng.
Bên cạnh đó, lãi suất phải được đánh giá bằng chi phí vay thực tế và khả năng tiếp cận vốn của doanh nghiệp.
Theo ông Lộc, bất động sản là lĩnh vực thường sử dụng vốn dài hạn, trong khi nguồn trả nợ của nhiều khoản vay phụ thuộc vào tiến độ dự án cũng như khả năng thanh khoản của thị trường. Nếu tín dụng tập trung vào dự án chậm triển khai, sản phẩm khó tiêu thụ hoặc mang tính đầu cơ, thời gian thu hồi vốn kéo dài, sức ép có thể lan sang chi phí vốn của cả danh mục cho vay.
Bên cạnh kiểm soát tín dụng vào các lĩnh vực tiềm ẩn rủi ro, ông Lộc nhấn mạnh ổn định kinh tế vĩ mô là nền tảng quan trọng để lãi suất giảm một cách thực chất là dựa trên nền tảng vĩ mô.
“Chính phủ cần sử dụng chính sách tài khóa và các giải pháp phía cung để hỗ trợ ổn định giá: tháo gỡ nút thắt sản xuất, bảo đảm giá cả năng lượng và hàng hóa thiết yếu, giảm chi phí logistics, cân nhắc lộ trình điều chỉnh giá những mặt hàng do Nhà nước quản lý. Bên cạnh đó, cần ưu tiên hiệu quả của đầu tư công, tiến độ và khả năng nâng năng lực sản xuất”, ông Lộc phân tích.
Bên cạnh đó, việc điều hành tỷ giá cần đủ linh hoạt để hấp thụ biến động từ bên ngoài. Không thể mặc định rằng trong mọi hoàn cảnh đều có thể đồng thời giữ tỷ giá gần như cố định, hạ mạnh lãi suất và mở rộng tín dụng nhanh.
TS Nguyễn Văn Lộc lưu ý, việc đánh giá hiệu quả giảm lãi suất không nên chỉ dựa trên mức lãi suất công bố của ngân hàng, mà cần xem xét chi phí vay thực tế, bao gồm các khoản phí bắt buộc, điều kiện áp dụng sau thời gian ưu đãi và khả năng tiếp cận vốn của từng nhóm khách hàng.

articles.title: Jensen Huang didn't show confidence in his successor, report says | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang described Colette Kress, the company’s CFO who has now replaced him as interim CEO, as “a deer in the headlights” during a presentation earlier in the summer, the Wall Street Journal reported, citing an anonymous source.
Huang made the comment during a meeting with Nvidia’s finance team about the company’s plans to provide guarantees worth billions of dollars to data center operators that couldn’t afford to buy its chips up front, according to the report.
He reportedly also said Kress was a person who couldn’t help him steer strategy or decision-making.
Kress has been with Nvidia for over 13 years now, after serving as SVP and CFO of Cisco’s Business Technology and Operations Finance. The report said she has questioned Nvidia’s program-focused, credit-based deals involving Huang’s son-in-law Nico Caprez, and wanted to know how to decide which deals are beneficial, how to value guarantees, and determine returns.
Earlier in the year, she had scaled back on Nvidia’s commitment for OpenAI’s ambitious Ohio data center project. The company was in talks to provide $250 billion in credit to OpenAI but ended up committing $105 billion.
Huang resigned Thursday after reports of two extramarital affairs, including one with the company’s VP for healthcare, Kimberly Powell. The company is also investigating a possible Chinese espionage plot.
After Huang’s resignation, Reuters reported that he was having a third affair with another employee. Nvidia is currently searching for a permanent CEO to replace Huang, who had the top job for over 33 years.

articles.title: ‘We need to really foster local champions’: Celonis’s Alexander Rinke
articles.text:
Thirty years ago, Europe’s GDP was roughly on par with the US, Alexander Rinke told TNW. Today it is dramatically less. The Celonis co-founder and co-CEO does not want AI to make that gap wider.
Rinke spoke to Cristian Dina for the TNW Podcast at HumanX in Amsterdam on 23 September. Earlier that day he had joined a panel on stage called “Can Europe Actually Build Sovereign AI?”. Earlier guests include Steve Lucas of Boomi, Arvind Jain of Glean, and Daniel Dines of UiPath. The full conversation is in the video below.
Local champions, not distrust
Countries and groups of countries such as Europe want control over parts of the AI stack, Rinke said. They want to know where their data and their IP go. Europe also needs its own companies to take part in an AI economy that will be huge.
“We need to really foster local champions, not because we don’t trust the Americans or we think AI is going to kill us all. Just because we want to make sure we take part of the upside.” Alexander Rinke, Celonis
Celonis is one example, he said. Its headquarters are in New York and Munich, and it has more than 20 offices around the world, with a strong presence in Germany, Spain and the UK. Europe is “not a satellite for us,” he said.
Owning the weights
For a company or a public agency, sovereign AI means owning its own AI, Rinke said. In the end, that means owning the model weights.
“They don’t want to give all of their data to any model to train on that data.” Alexander Rinke, Celonis
Every organisation is like a snowflake, he said, so its processes and their context are unique. That needs open platforms that can be installed in sovereign environments. Celonis keeps a customer’s process data with the customer and does not send it anywhere. It also helps customers tune open-source models for specific business tasks. For those tasks, he said, they can get the same or better results than with frontier models.
An x-ray for business processes
Rinke started Celonis 15 years ago with his co-founders, Martin Klenk and Bastian Nominacher. They first wanted to build models that could simulate how a business works. To feed a simulation, they needed to know how the business ran today, and companies could not tell them.
“So we built an x-ray machine that looks at the data the business generates and x-rays how the processes work.” Alexander Rinke, Celonis
Celonis now calls this process intelligence. It maps how work really gets done, across systems and outside them, so companies can redesign it with AI. The company has about 3,500 people, he said.
Celonis recently bought Ikigai Labs, an MIT spin-off. Ikigai builds specialised models for tabular and time-series data and for what-if simulation. A large language model can use them as a tool, Rinke said, for jobs such as forecasting a supply chain or deciding whether to settle an insurance claim.
Asked about an IPO or new funding, Rinke spoke about the next phase of growth instead. He pointed to the Context Model that Celonis launched and to the Ikigai deal. Celonis describes the Context Model as a living model of a business in motion, built from its operational data and connected to its strategy.
Product-market fit is easy to claim
Many startup pitches claim product-market fit that the company does not have, Rinke said. His test has four questions. Is the product valuable? Is it uniquely valuable, or easy to replace? Is it repeatable, or custom each time? Will customers keep paying for it?
“It’s easy to say that you have. It’s very easy to put on a slide for VCs.” Alexander Rinke, Celonis
If the answer to all four is yes, the next step is what he calls product-market-people fit: the organisation needed to scale it. Scaling too early can grow revenue that does not last, he said, especially in a boom market like AI.
Celonis was his first real venture. The founders started it during their studies, and Rinke put his master’s on hold and never finished it. They bootstrapped for five years, and winning the first enterprise clients without references was very hard, he said.
Build for customers, not rounds
Venture capital is a good idea if a company wants to move quickly, Rinke said. But it does not replace the work a bootstrapped company has to do.
“You shouldn’t build the company to raise capital. You should build the company for customers.” Alexander Rinke, Celonis
He now works much more closely with Celonis engineers than he did a few years ago. He oversees some technical projects himself and is involved in how the company adopts AI internally. Asked whether he is technical, he said: “Yeah, pretty technical.”

articles.title: CMF’s milk carton-shaped Bluetooth speaker is down to a new low price
articles.text:
Bluetooth speakers are often boring boxes in plain colors, but not this one! As part of Nothing’s ongoing early Black Friday promo, you can grab its unique, milk carton-shaped CMF Speaker S from Amazon and Nothing for just $39. That’s a solid $20 discount and the lowest price we’ve seen on Nothing’s newfangled wireless speaker, which hit the market about a month ago.
CMF’s milk carton-shaped Bluetooth speaker is down to a new low price
Nothing’s funky, compact Bluetooth speaker launched in October and is already on sale ahead of Black Friday.
The CMF Speaker S is the smaller of the two recently-released models — the larger Series M is also on sale at Amazon for $79 ($30 off) — and sports a 45mm driver with two passive radiators to help with low-end frequencies. It can run for up to 18 hours on a single charge and carries an IP68 rating for water and dust resistance. Despite its carefree aesthetic, it also supports stereo pairing with a second Seris S speaker, Bluetooth 6, fast pairing via multiple methods (including NFC and Google Fast Pair), and audio over USB-C.
In addition to their great sound and compact footprint, both the Speaker S and Speaker M feature removable faceplates and multifunction front knobs. Not only can you swap them out to customize the colors, but CMF plans to share STL files so anyone with a 3D printer can create their own attachments and looks.

articles.title: Why Apple's HomeView relies so heavily on your iPhone - Engadget
articles.text:
Why Apple's HomeView relies so heavily on your iPhone
It all comes down to convenience and personalization without sacrificing privacy.
"There's no product in the world better designed to be your intelligent personal hub than iPhone."
That's the statement newly minted Apple CEO John Ternus made during his opening remarks at his first iPhone event this year. It should be no surprise then, that the device holding so much of your data would play a vital role with a separate "intelligent personal hub" that stays inside your home.
This week marks the arrival of the HomeView, Apple's long-rumored smart display that was announced last month. As I explained in detail in my review, it's basically a combination of several gadgets in one. It's both a visual interface and a smart speaker that is always listening for your Siri queries. It's a smart home hub for a range of connected devices. It's a sous chef in the kitchen, and it's a FaceTime station when you need to catch up with friends and family. Heck, it's even a digital photo frame.
The HomeView doesn't run apps though. It performs all those functions, and more, by mirroring the apps that you have on your iPhone or iPad. Instead of allowing you to download software from the App Store, the HomeView's system works like CarPlay does in your car. It shows you the compatible apps you've already installed on your phone or tablet, as well as Apple's core suite, including Calendar, Messages, Reminders and Weather.
This is just one of the reasons an iPhone (or iPad) needs to be close by for the HomeView to work.
"When we design home products, we always keep three things in mind," Cecilia Dantas, a member of Apple's Home product marketing team, told me. "They have to be intelligent, personal and private."
Since Siri AI needs all those apps to be able to provide the very personal context that makes its answers more intelligent and conversational, Apple needed a way to grant it that access that didn't compromise your privacy. Having your iPhone be the only container for that information and requiring it to be around for your data to be accessible helps keep it safe from prying eyes when you're away.
As a more general home hub, the HomeView has to work for every member of your household so they can turn lights off or see who's at the door. But it shouldn't be showing them every text message you get from your parents or revealing your calendar invites and inadvertently ruining surprises. This privacy is why, in addition to the built-in face and voice recognition, the HomeView relies so heavily on an iPhone or iPad.
"Everything that feels natural on a phone is now available in a subtle, glanceable device that gives you what you need in the moment," VP of hardware engineering Matthew Costello said. "It recognizes you and shows you your information, but when you step away, it's gone."
Costello further explained that the HomeView offers the best combination of personal information with the convenience of a dedicated communal device. Since the iPhone is a user's hub for their personal content — and really, their life — it only made sense to "extend and link that intelligence" into products like the HomeView.
If the HomeView doesn't recognize a user, it will only allow them to perform basic tasks. And even if you are a recognized user, you'll need to have your recently unlocked iPhone or iPad nearby for the smart display to show things like your Messages or Calendar.
"Personal information only surfaces once you've been recognized by your face, and [if] your paired iPhone is present and recently unlocked," Costello noted. "We thought building on the contextual information and the intelligence, but also the privacy, was super critical and also very unique."
By tying what shows up for you on the HomeView to your phone, your data is displayed while you're interacting with the device and disappears with you when you do. As Costello explained, it's not "posted on or housed on the device in any way."
The heavy reliance on an iPhone or an iPad has additional benefits. Like you can on a HomePod, the HomeView allows you to hand off music, FaceTime calls and more. One of the device's best features is recipe integration in Safari that makes cooking easier. It's also powered by the hand off action, so you need that other Apple device to kickstart the process. But Dantas explained that Apple doesn't see reliance on your phone or tablet as a hindrance.
"It's not just dependency, it's also part of this ecosystem," she said. The HomeView's similarity to your phone doesn't just enable familiar apps, but also a familiar method of interaction.
Speaking of interaction, there's a reason why there aren't any buttons on the HomeView. Apple intentionally built it like this. I found it odd, considering the device is a bit of a hybrid of an iPad (touchscreen), an Apple Watch (square shape) and a HomePod (speaker), two of which have physical buttons. But Costello said touch input was always meant to be secondary.
"We always envisioned it as something that was voice first, then touch second," he explained. "As we [designed] the product, that's how we thought about it, so that eliminated buttons and physical controls."
For Dantas, one of the main challenges during the product development phase was restraint. The process of bringing a new product and new software to life was obviously a tall task, but the engineering team also had to determine which parts of Apple's existing devices and services to include and which ones to leave behind.
"We've had home products for a while, and we built on that foundation," she said. "I think it was really, really challenging to go through and decide what do we bring and what do we not bring [to the HomeView]. That was very intentional to deliver this experience that's powerful and that's simple."

articles.title: Giá vàng giảm không phanh, kịch bản lùi về 2.890 USD được nhắc tới
articles.text:
Thị trường vàng thế giới trải qua những phiên giao dịch biến động mạnh khi áp lực bán gia tăng, kéo giá kim loại quý xuống dưới ngưỡng tâm lý 4.000 USD/ounce.
Đằng sau đà giảm là sự cộng hưởng của nhiều yếu tố: kỳ vọng chính sách tiền tệ Mỹ tiếp tục thắt chặt, đồng USD và lợi suất trái phiếu đi lên, trong khi các tín hiệu phân tích kỹ thuật cũng phát đi cảnh báo về nguy cơ giá vàng điều chỉnh sâu hơn.
CPI Mỹ cao hơn dự báo, kỳ vọng lãi suất thay đổi
Tâm điểm gây sức ép lên giá vàng là báo cáo lạm phát tháng 10 của Mỹ. Theo Cục Thống kê Lao động Mỹ (BLS), chỉ số giá tiêu dùng (CPI) tăng 0,4% so với tháng trước, cao hơn mức dự báo 0,3% của giới phân tích, trong khi lạm phát lõi cũng neo ở mức 0,3% tháng thứ ba liên tiếp.
Diễn biến trên khiến thị trường lo ngại Cục Dự trữ Liên bang Mỹ (Fed) có thể tiếp tục nâng lãi suất trong cuộc họp tháng 12, thậm chí cân nhắc mức tăng mạnh hơn thông thường.
Thị trường chủ yếu nghiêng về kịch bản Fed tăng lãi suất thêm 0,25 điểm phần trăm trong cuộc họp tháng 12. Tuy nhiên, số liệu lạm phát cao hơn dự báo đã khiến giới đầu tư tính đến khả năng Fed có thể hành động mạnh tay hơn, với mức tăng 0,5 điểm phần trăm.
Theo công cụ CME FedWatch tại thời điểm ngày 11/11, xác suất Fed tăng lãi suất 0,5 điểm phần trăm trong cuộc họp tháng 12 được thị trường định giá ở mức 13,2%, trong khi khả năng tăng 0,25 điểm phần trăm là 86,8%.
Trước đó, Thống đốc Fed Christopher Waller cho rằng cơ quan này nên cân nhắc mức tăng 0,5 điểm phần trăm nếu CPI lõi tháng 10 tăng từ 0,3% trở lên.
Hệ quả là lợi suất trái phiếu kho bạc Mỹ, đặc biệt là trái phiếu kỳ hạn 2 năm, tăng mạnh; đồng USD cũng lên giá, qua đó tạo thêm sức ép lên vàng - tài sản không sinh lãi.
"Phòng tuyến" 4.000 USD và nỗi lo sụt giảm sâu hơn
Việc để mất mốc 4.000 USD/ounce không chỉ là một tổn thất về mặt tâm lý. Giới phân tích kỹ thuật coi đây là "phòng tuyến" then chốt và việc giá đóng cửa dưới ngưỡng này được xem là tín hiệu tiêu cực, có thể kích hoạt một làn sóng bán tháo mới từ các quỹ đầu cơ.
Ông Fawad Razaqzada, chuyên gia tại FOREX.com, nhận định vùng 3.942-4.000 USD là "hỗ trợ then chốt"; nếu bị phá vỡ một cách thuyết phục, nó sẽ phủ nhận đà tăng ngắn hạn và mở ra không gian giảm giá sâu hơn.
Các mốc hỗ trợ tiếp theo đang bị đe dọa gồm 3.950 USD và 3.925 USD; sâu hơn nữa, ngân hàng Canada TD Securities dự báo vàng có thể kiểm tra lại vùng 3.900 USD.
Trong kịch bản xấu nhất, chuyên gia Razaqzada chỉ ra mục tiêu tiếp theo là đáy gần nhất quanh 3.870 USD và nếu mất luôn mốc này, vùng hỗ trợ kỹ thuật tiếp theo sẽ là 3.738 USD.
Đáng chú ý hơn cả là cảnh báo kỹ thuật từ HSBC Trinkaus & Burkhardt, khi giới phân tích chỉ ra rằng trên biểu đồ tuần, vàng đang đứng trước nguy cơ hoàn tất một mô hình vai - đầu - vai (head and shoulders) kinh điển.
Cấu trúc này gồm 3 đỉnh: vai trái quanh tháng 10/2025, đầu là đỉnh cao nhất vào tháng 1-2/2026 và vai phải hình thành trong giai đoạn tháng 8-9/2026, với đường viền cổ (neckline) nằm ở vùng 3.886-3.942 USD/ounce.
Đáng chú ý, giá vàng có thời điểm đóng cửa ở mức 3.872,86 USD, tức đã xuyên thủng vùng viền cổ 3.886-3.942 USD, xác nhận tín hiệu phá vỡ (breakdown) bước đầu.
Theo một phân tích kỹ thuật khác trên TradingView, nếu đà phá vỡ này được duy trì, mô hình vai - đầu - vai mở ra mục tiêu đo đếm kỹ thuật (measured target) quanh 3.252 USD.
Trước đó, Peter Brandt cảnh báo mô hình vai - đầu - vai trên biểu đồ tuần có thể mở ra khả năng giá vàng lùi về 2.890 USD/ounce nếu vùng hỗ trợ 4.100-4.200 USD bị xuyên thủng. Ông lưu ý đây là kịch bản kỹ thuật, không phải dự báo chắc chắn.
Sự kết hợp giữa tín hiệu trên biểu đồ tuần và biểu đồ quý khiến HSBC cảnh báo giá vàng đang ở trong vùng nhạy cảm. HSBC ví von vàng đang bước trên “tảng băng mỏng”, hàm ý áp lực giảm có thể gia tăng nếu các ngưỡng hỗ trợ quan trọng bị xuyên thủng.
Nếu mô hình vai - đầu - vai được xác nhận, đây có thể là tín hiệu cho thấy nhịp điều chỉnh của vàng còn tiếp diễn. Áp lực từ dữ liệu lạm phát Mỹ, kỳ vọng Fed duy trì chính sách tiền tệ thắt chặt và đồng USD mạnh lên cũng là những yếu tố bất lợi đối với kim loại quý.
Thị trường vàng lúc này đang đứng trước những luồng thông tin trái chiều. Một bên là áp lực bán tháo từ kỳ vọng Fed diều hâu và sức mạnh của đồng USD. Bên kia là lực cầu bền bỉ từ các ngân hàng trung ương và dòng tiền đầu cơ đang tìm kiếm cơ hội giá rẻ.
Kịch bản về một đợt giảm về vùng 3.900-3.870 USD và sâu hơn là hoàn toàn có cơ sở, đặc biệt khi mô hình "vai - đầu - vai" vẫn đang lơ lửng như một lời cảnh báo. Nhà đầu tư cần hết sức thận trọng trước những biến động khó lường.

articles.title: Here’s how you can save on your GTA VI preorder ahead of launch
articles.text:
The long-awaited launch of GTA VI is around the corner, happening next Friday, November 19th. While discounts on the game itself will be rare for some time, there’s a clever workaround to save you a few bucks on your digital copy. We found discounts on gift cards for both Sony PlayStation and Microsoft Xbox Series S/X owners to help shave some dollars off your upcoming trip to Vice City. You can pick up a $75 Sony gift card for $69 at Newegg when you use coupon code BNWF2669 at checkout, and Costco members can pick up four $25 Sony gift cards for $89.99.
Here’s how you can save on your GTA VI preorder ahead of launch
Preloading is already underway for Rockstar’s anticipated open-world game, but you’re not too late to save.
Meanwhile, Xbox owners can pick up a $90 Xbox gift card for $80 at Newegg by using the coupon code BNWF2662 at checkout. The GTA VI standard edition is $79.99, while the ultimate edition is $99.99, so you can either spend an extra $10 out of pocket for the upgrade, or buy the standard version and set any leftover credit aside for use later on.

articles.title: Bloomberg details web of Chinese AI companies with smuggled NVIDIA chips linked to Alice Huang - Engadget
articles.text:
Bloomberg details web of Chinese AI companies with smuggled NVIDIA chips linked to Alice Huang
The NVIDIA chips involved are banned in China.
A Chinese company with ties to Alice Huang procured NVIDIA AI chips banned in the country, which were then installed at a Shanghai AI facility that also has ties to Alice Huang, according to Bloomberg. The publication says the documents it has reviewed for its report shows explicit evidence that there's a network of Chinese companies, which have managed to get their hands on NVIDIA chips that weren't supposed to be sold in China, with Huang at the center.
US officials believe that Alice Huang is a spy recruited by China's main intelligence agency to target NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang. The goal was apparently to learn more about America's AI plans and to get Jensen Huang to persuade the US government to let his company ship its more advanced chips to China. Before he stepped down as CEO of NVIDIA, Jensen Huang reportedly admitted in a staff memo that he had an affair with Alice Huang.
To the public, Alice was an executive at Singaporean company Megaspeed, but the reports that had come out since the issue blew up paint a different picture of who she truly was. Bloomberg says the NVIDIA chips listed in the documents it reviewed were sold to Aperia Cloud Services, an NVIDIA Cloud Partner in Singapore. Aperia purchased 22 servers from Dell containing NVIDIA H800 chips, which are banned in China. According to the report, Dell cut off business ties with Aperia in February 2025 due to concerns around the deal.
Bloomberg found the hardware details in filings from a company called Shanghai Longteng Intelligent Computing, which was set up by Alice a decade ago. They were documented as part of the information the company had to submit to the Chinese government, since it was using its servers as a collateral for financing. While Alice hasn't been part of Shanghai Longteng since 2017 — and the documents didn't say if she was personally involved in the procurement of the chips — Huang Yu, who was identified as her sister, was the one who took over as majority owner. The filings also revealed that the company's servers included 52 units made by Super Micro Computer Inc. Those units were equipped with NVIDIA's H100 or H200 chips, which can't be sold to Chinese companies without express permission from the US government.
The Shanghai AI facility where the smuggled NVIDIA units were installed is called the Yangtze River Delta Project, which Bloomberg says also has ties to Alice Huang. Its president is Kang Wei, who is being reported as Alice's husband and the person who introduced her to Jensen Huang. Alice's company Megaspeed also presented a rendering of the Yangtze River Delta Project to its investors in 2024 and claimed that it was its largest AI facility. Former NVIDIA-CEO Jensen Huang is due to testify before Congress this month, and it's likely all of this information will be pored over by officials in the run-up to the event.

articles.title: Cornelis launches CN6000 800G networking to rival Nvidia InfiniBand
articles.text:
Cornelis, which Intel spun out in 2020, has launched CN6000, a family of 800G network cards and switches for AI and supercomputers. It claims lower latency than Nvidia’s InfiniBand, based on its own tests. Partner systems arrive in early 2027.
Cornelis, a networking company spun out of Intel, has launched CN6000, a family of 800G network cards and switches for AI clusters and supercomputers, it announced this week. It is pitching them as a rival to Nvidia’s InfiniBand.
In large AI systems, thousands of chips must constantly swap data. If the network is slow, expensive chips sit idle. “Every minute an accelerator waits on the network is capacity our customers paid for and didn’t use,” said CEO Lisa Spelman.
The main card uses Omni-Path, a networking technology Intel dropped in 2019 before spinning the business off as Cornelis in 2020. Cornelis says the card can handle 1.6 billion messages a second. It also says it is 21% faster than Nvidia’s InfiniBand at passing a small message, though that comes from its own tests.
A faster single message does not mean jobs finish 21% sooner, since that depends on the workload. Cornelis also launched a card for standard Ethernet networks, which most AI data centres use, with support for the newer Ultra Ethernet standard due later.
The cards work with chips from AMD, Intel, Nvidia and Qualcomm. Dell, Lenovo and Supermicro are among the server makers planning to support them, with systems due in early 2027.
Networking has become a hot spot in AI. Nvidia has spent billions on optical links, Huawei is betting on wiring over chips, and startups such as Upscale AI are building ways to connect rival chips. AMD, a Cornelis partner, is also building rack-scale systems to compete with Nvidia.

articles.title: You can adjust the position of the trackball on Keychron’s new wireless mouse
articles.text:
The Nape Pro was Keychron’s first trackball device that was introduced at CES 2026 with a slim and compact design allowing it to be positioned right up against a keyboard. The company’s new T1 HE instead looks more like other trackball mice already available from companies like Logitech and Kensington with a 34mm ball positioned on the side to improve ergonomics. But since hands and fingers come in various sizes, the T1 HE allows the position of its trackball to be fine-tuned with minor positional adjustments so it rests squarely under your thumb without any reaching.
You can adjust the position of the trackball on Keychron’s new wireless mouse
A pair of dials underneath the T1 HE let you fine-tune where its trackball is positioned under your thumb.
The T1 HE is now available for preorder through Keychron’s online store for $59.99 in black, white, or translucent color options. Shipping is expected to start in early December. A pair of dials on the underside of the mouse are used to adjust the vertical and horizontal position of the trackball, which can also be extended or retracted. The adjustments are limited to just a few millimeters in either direction, but those minor improvements to ergonomics could go a long way to making the T1 HE more comfortable to use on a regular basis.
The sensitivity of the T1 HE’s optical sensor can be adjusted from 100 DPI to 2,400 DPI using a button that cycles through presets or the Keychron Launcher software that also allows for other customizations including button remapping and creating macros. The mouse features six customizable buttons in total, and a 600mAh battery good for up to 106 hours of use in Bluetooth mode, or 98 hours when using an included 2.4GHz wireless receiver. If you don’t want to worry about charging, the T1 HE Wireless Adjustable Trackball Mouse can also be used with a USB-C cable.

articles.title: Google's Gemini can now read your Google Wallet to help you budget
articles.text:
Google is rolling out a Google Wallet connection to all Gemini app users in the US. Gemini can analyse spending, find subscriptions and suggest budgets, with read-only access. Google says it may train AI on summaries of that data if users keep activity on.
Google is letting every Gemini app user in the US connect Google Wallet, so the chatbot can answer questions about their spending, the company announced on Thursday. Users can also link bank and credit card accounts through Plaid for more detailed answers.
After tagging @Google Wallet in a chat, users can ask Gemini to chart last quarter’s spending or help them save $1,000. It can also find subscriptions that went up in price, or use last year’s spending to suggest a holiday budget.
The connection is opt-in and read-only. Gemini can see account data but cannot move, manage or invest money, and users can switch it off at any time. That differs from Google’s Universal Cart, which already lets Gemini take payments.
Google says it does not train its AI directly on Wallet data. But its help pages say that if users keep their Gemini activity on, it may train on summaries of their transactions. Some of those chats may also be read by human reviewers.
Google also launched Memory Summary, a page showing what Gemini remembers about a user, such as their goals and preferences. Users can edit or delete those details. It is not available in Europe or the UK.
Google’s rivals got there first. OpenAI began letting some ChatGPT users link bank accounts in May, and Anthropic launched a similar read-only finance feature for Claude last week. Google recently changed its privacy policy so that connected Gmail and Photos data can shape ads.

articles.title: Whoop Humans is a social network designed for fitness enthusiasts - Engadget
articles.text:
Whoop Humans is a social network designed for fitness enthusiasts
Members can only share data from their Whoop wearables as guarantee of authenticity.
Whoop, the company behind the popular screenless wearable trackers, has launched a social network for users who like sharing their exercise details and fitness efforts called Whoop Humans. It's a rather unusual name, so you might be wondering how the company decided on it. Well, Will Ahmed, the CEO of Whoop, described it as the "most verifiably human network ever launched." Members can share their fitness data on the social network, including their sleep, recovery, strain and activities information. In all cases, the data comes from a Whoop wearable. That's "real-world information that cannot simply be generated as a conventional text post" at a time when "traditional social networks are increasingly filled with artificial content," the company said in its announcement.
Whoop already has Teams, which connects users through groups and leaderboards. But the new social network lets users follow friends and family directly to comment and react to their posts. The company envisions a social network, wherein people can check in on each other based on their progress. The idea is for members to be able to congratulate each other when they reach their goals or to be able to remind a friend to take it easy if they see the other's "Recovery" data is low. Hard to imagine most people taking an interest in another's fitness information, but people who are very much into fitness might see value in the social network.
In addition to being able to share fitness data, members will also be able to share photos from their workouts with a feature called "Moments." They can keep those Moments private, however, and, thankfully, they can choose which workout types or achievements appear on the social network. Just because they're wearing a Whoop doesn't mean their data will automatically be shared. Members can still update their sharing preferences any time they want. Whoop Humans is now live and available through the company's app.

articles.title: Jensen Huang was reckless with the environment, too
articles.text:
Under cofounder Jensen Huang, Nvidia has become the engine for the AI boom — and one of the tech industry’s biggest environmental liabilities. Its sought-after chips have triggered a new wave of water- and chemical-intensive factories, drained power grids from inside massive data centers, and set the stage for a looming e-waste problem.
Jensen Huang was reckless with the environment, too
Nvidia’s environmental footprint extends way beyond its own offices.
Under Huang’s leadership, Nvidia clashed with environmental groups seeking to hold the company accountable for its so-called “hidden” emissions. Huang has talked up the idea of using AI to fight climate change while his company’s supply chain emissions ballooned. Nvidia’s investments, meanwhile, have supported the buildout of data centers that have sparked intense backlash for both their local and global impact. Now, after the CEO’s shocking resignation amid a sprawling sex-and-espionage scandal, advocates are urging Nvidia to turn the page.
He compared AI to a surgeon who has “to cut you open to save you.”
“Jensen Huang has failed to put climate responsibility at the heart of the company’s growth strategy, to slow down the unchecked expansion of data centres or to prevent its chips from being deployed in unethical applications like automated warfare,” Avex Li, Greenpeace East Asia’s project lead for AI supply chain campaign, said in a press release Thursday. The organization is now pushing interim CEO Colette Kress to commit Nvidia to decarbonizing by investing in renewable energy, as well as ensuring its technology is used in a way that “respects human rights.” Nvidia didn’t immediately respond to requests for comment from The Verge.
Huang has projected optimism about how AI can boost the adoption of renewable energy, even as the planet-heating emissions of tech companies — including his own — have grown in the generative AI era. “If you want to turn a corner on climate change, if you want a future that’s sustainable, lean into A.I. It is the best opportunity we have to get there,” Huang said in a September episode of The Ezra Klein Show, arguing that electricity demand for AI is leading companies to buy more sustainable energy.
In the same interview, however, he admitted data centers will rely on more fossil fuels in the near term, and that building up the infrastructure for AI will likely result in “an enormous amount of pain and suffering.” He compared AI to a surgeon who has “to cut you open to save you.”
Nvidia’s supply-chain emissions have grown 725 percent since 2020, according to an analysis of the company’s public disclosures by research analyst Ketan Joshi and several environmental organizations, including Greenpeace and Climate Action Against Disinformation, published in September. It’s an increase of about 9.4 million metric tons of planet-heating pollution, roughly equivalent to the emissions from nearly 25 gas plants over a year. Supply chain emissions the company disclosed for fiscal year 2026 reached around 10.7 million metric tons of CO2, according to Nvidia’s latest sustainability report.
Joshi and his co-authors approximated how much greenhouse gas pollution comes from the use of chips the company sells, a category Nvidia doesn’t include in its sustainability reports. Those emissions could have reached 21 million metric tons in 2025, according to the report, based on estimated chip power consumption. That level of pollution puts Nvidia on par with Russia’s state-owned coal company, according to Joshi.
Those “indirect” emissions — from its supply chain and the use of its products — make up the bulk of Nvidia’s climate impact. The carbon footprint of facilities Nvidia actually owns and operates looks much smaller in comparison because Nvidia designs chips that other companies like TSMC then manufacture. Greenhouse gas emissions coming directly from Nvidia-operated facilities and vehicles only reached 9,822 metric tons in fiscal year 2026, the company’s sustainability report shows. And in 2025, the company reached a goal of matching 100 percent of its facilities’ electricity use with clean energy purchases.
Greenpeace wants Nvidia to extend that goal to its entire manufacturing supply chain. When Greenpeace activists disrupted Huang’s speech at Nvidia GTC in Berlin last month, he responded onstage by saying, “I’ll talk to you guys later … All important issues, but let me get through my keynote.” In the Thursday press release, Greenpeace says Nvidia has yet to meet with Greenpeace despite the organization’s attempts to “seek dialogue” with the company over the past two years.
“One of Huang’s defining legacies is inflating a speculative AI bubble, pouring billions of dollars into infrastructure with little regard for the real-world consequences inflicted on local communities and the climate,” Katrin Wu, Big Tech campaigner at Greenpeace International, said in an email to The Verge. “Huang may be gone, but the ‘tech colonialism’ Nvidia perpetuates continues.”
“Huang may be gone, but the ‘tech colonialism’ Nvidia perpetuates continues.”
Beyond Nvidia’s day-to-day operations, Huang threw his weight around as the CEO of one of the world’s most valuable companies — chumming it up with President Donald Trump and lobbying for the US to allow sales of its powerful chips to China. The company’s influence on the global economy extended beyond chips as it invested in data centers stocking its GPUs.
And with electricity supply often the thorniest bottleneck to building more and bigger data centers, Nvidia’s long tendrils reached into the energy sector as well. NVentures, the company’s venture capital arm, has funded battery recycling company Redwood Materials and startups developing AI tools to optimize power grids and make data centers more responsive to fluctuations in energy demand.
Nvidia joined one of those startups, Emerald AI, along with Google to cofound the AI Energy Management Alliance (AEMA) in September. The alliance advocates for strategies that tech companies promote as ways to keep data centers from overwhelming power grids or raising utility bills for other customers, including generating power on-site and making “flexible” facilities that can pause operations during times of peak energy demand. Notably, some environmental groups argue that those measures might just help data centers come online faster without fully insulating households from the impact that rising electricity demand has on their air quality or utility bills.
Whether Nvidia’s environmental footprint shrinks or expands from here will depend on whoever steps in to fill Huang’s shoes. Over the years, Greenpeace and other environmental groups have pointed out that despite having an outsize impact on the environment, Nvidia doesn’t necessarily come under the same public scrutiny as more consumer-facing brands like Apple or Google. Huang’s exploits have thrust the company into a new kind of spotlight, however, just as data centers increasingly face backlash from nearby communities. Nvidia won’t be able to hide from the glare.

articles.title: BYD admits wheel assembly error on its flagship electric SUV - Engadget
articles.text:
BYD admits wheel assembly error on its flagship electric SUV
Some Great Tang SUVs had their wheels installed the wrong way.
BYD has apologized for an assembly mistake affecting some units of its newly released Great Tang — or Datang, as it's called in China — electric SUV. According to Bloomberg, several owners complained that the wider wheel rims that were supposed to be installed on the rear of the vehicle were installed on the front. Meanwhile, the narrower wheel rims for the front of the car were installed on the back instead.
The Chinese electric automaker has posted its apology on social network Weibo, explaining that it launched an investigation after getting complaints from owners. Apparently, it traced the problem to its Hubei-based wheel mesh assembly supplier. BYD said it has already fixed the issue, and the supplier has also added a visual inspection mechanism on the production line, so that future vehicles will no longer be affected.
BYD didn't say how many vehicles were affected by the assembly error, but it said that there was no safety risk associated with the wheels being installed the wrong way. Even so, it will replace the wheel rims of the those vehicles for free and will also offer their owners a replacement vehicle or compensation for what they will spend on transportation while their Great Tang SUVs are being repaired. In addition, the company will restart their vehicle's warranty period.
The company unveiled the Great Tang SUV in March, with prices starting at around $40,000. It received 150,000 orders in its home country. BYD is planning to release the electric vehicle in European and Asian markets outside China by the end of this year or in early 2027.

articles.title: GridAI to buy Wyoming gas firm Pronghorn to power AI data centres
articles.text:
GridAI Technologies has agreed to buy Wyoming natural gas producer Pronghorn Resources in an all-stock deal. It plans to build gas-fired power plants for AI data centres, aiming for 300 MW in 2027, but has no named customers yet.
GridAI Technologies has agreed to buy Pronghorn Resources, a natural gas producer in Wyoming, to power AI data centres, the company announced on Thursday. It aims to deliver its first 300 MW of power in 2027.
Pronghorn produces nearly 100 million cubic feet of gas a day from about 3,200 wells in the Powder River Basin. It also owns more than 450 miles of pipelines and has rights to nearly 1 million acres of land and minerals.
GridAI plans to build gas-fired power plants that feed data centres directly, so customers do not have to wait years for a grid connection. It says Pronghorn’s current gas could fuel about 600 MW of power, but that is an estimate. The plants still need to be built and paid for.
The deal is paid in shares, not cash. Pronghorn’s owners will get about 1.25 million GridAI shares plus preferred stock, and the deal is expected to close by 22 November. GridAI, which trades on Nasdaq, was worth about $31M in October, according to StockAnalysis.
GridAI is also taking Wyoming rights to a planned small nuclear reactor design, though it says gas remains its focus for now. It has not named any customers. Last week, Crusoe gave up its Wyoming site to Google, reportedly after failing to find enough customers.
Wyoming is drawing AI investment as other places push back. Google plans a $17B data centre there that will run mainly on gas. Meanwhile, US voters rejected data centres in 40 of 41 local ballot measures this month, as AI fuels a gas-plant boom.

articles.title: The smallest version of Camp Snap’s retro digital camcorder fits on your keychain
articles.text:
Last week, Camp Snap launched a miniaturized version of its screen-free CS-8 video camera that was half the size of the original with a smaller grip designed to be easier for kids to hold. But it turns out the company wasn’t done shrinking its hardware. Camp Snap’s new CS-8 Micro is even smaller than the CS-8 Mini. It’s around three inches long and weighs just 1.5 ounces so you can hang it from your keys and, like its larger predecessors, it can capture video using one of five built-in filters.
The smallest version of Camp Snap’s retro digital camcorder fits on your keychain
The Camp Snap CS-8 Micro is just three inches long and adds a tiny LCD screen that’s only used as a viewfinder.
The CS-8 Micro will be available starting on November 17th at 11AM ET through Camp Snap’s online store, Target, and Urban Outfitters for $39.99, and similar to the collectible Kodak Charmera, the Micro is being sold in sealed mystery boxes. Colors like hot pink, lilac, lime, and orange will be easier to find, while vintage classic (black) and glow in the dark will be much rarer.
Unlike the original CS-8 and CS-8 Mini, the new Micro does include an LCD display, but it’s only used as a viewfinder. You can’t watch, edit, or delete anything you’ve captured on the camera itself. You need to transfer the videos to a phone or computer using a USB-C cable to enjoy them, or move its included 4GB microSD into a card reader.
As Camp Snap has been progressively shrinking its retro camcorder, it’s also reduced its resolution. The original captured videos at 4K, while the CS-8 Mini did 2.7K. The CS-8 Micro is limited to 720p, but carries forward features like an 8x digital zoom and a selection of five filters that include vintage effects that add flicker and grain to emulate the look of 8mm film. Camp Snap estimates the Micro’s 4GB microSD card can hold 45 to 6o minutes of video, while its battery life is estimated to be 30 to 45 minutes on a full charge.
Correction, November 13th: The Camp Snap CS-8 Mini will launch on November 17th.

articles.title: Disney is now embracing the AI it once fought, from cartoons to finance
articles.text:
Disney will bring Ozzy Fox, a kids’ series animated with AI tools, to Disney+ in December, Bloomberg reported. Under CEO Josh D’Amaro, it is also using AI in finance, streaming suggestions and its parks, while still guarding its characters.
Disney, which once sued AI companies over its characters, is now putting the technology to work across the company, Bloomberg reported. In December, it will bring Ozzy Fox, a children’s series animated with AI, to Disney+.
Ozzy Fox was made with French startup Animaj, whose tools turn artists’ drawings and text instructions into 3D animation. It first appeared on YouTube in July, where some viewers called it “AI slop”.
The push is led by CEO Josh D’Amaro, who took over this year. A week into his tenure, OpenAI shut down its Sora video app, ending a planned deal for Disney to license its characters to it.
“We’re being very aggressive about exploring emerging technologies,” D’Amaro said at a company event this month.
Disney is building an AI tool to automate budget reports and testing AI viewing suggestions with some US Disney+ subscribers, according to Bloomberg. Patent filings describe AI characters that chat with park guests and microphones that hear when rides need repair.
In September, Disney named Character.AI’s chief executive, Karandeep Anand, as its first CTO. It has since bid $20M for some of the assets of the bankrupt chatbot startup, which could one day let Disney+ users talk to characters.
Disney still guards its characters closely. Rather than license them to AI firms, it has signed a deal letting Adobe build AI models on them under its control.

articles.title: The new Apple TV has a YouTube problem
articles.text:
People who received the brand new Apple TV 4k today saw some strange error messages as soon as they opened the YouTube app. As the first units arrived, the app was initially only showing a black screen with a QR code and an error message saying “YouTube is not yet available on this device.” In some cases the app was functional, but had a transparent red bar stuck at the bottom of the screen saying, “YouTube app is approved for device testing only and not for production use.”
The new Apple TV has a YouTube problem
A software update and a reboot should get YouTube working on your new Apple TV 4K.
Installing the new tvOS 27.2 update and rebooting wasn’t enough to resolve the issue for The Verge’s Tom Warren, he also had to uninstall and reinstall the app.
The Verge’s John Higgins said in his review of the new Apple TV 4K that it’s “one of the best streaming devices available,” but expensive compared to other streaming boxes.

articles.title: Bessent says anyone at Nvidia should answer for chips reaching China
articles.text:
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent says the Nvidia scandal should be about AI chips reaching China, not Jensen Huang’s private life. On Friday he asked whether Nvidia checked its customers. Anyone at the company should be held accountable, he said.
Bessent was speaking on CNBC’s “Squawk Box”. CNBC asked whether Nvidia’s top processors had reached China through Megaspeed, a Singapore-based Nvidia customer. Bessent said there was “a lot of leakage in the system”. The government is working to close it down, he added.
“The story has been thus far on Jensen Huang’s personal foibles,” Bessent said. “The real story here should be: Did Nvidia know their client, and was there a robust effort at Nvidia to make sure that there was no leakage and that they were selling to what were obviously pass-through shell companies?”
“I think it’s important that anyone at the company there be held accountable for that,” he said.
Huang resigned as Nvidia’s CEO on Thursday. He had admitted an affair with Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed executive. US officials suspect she is a Chinese intelligence asset.
Megaspeed and Nvidia’s chips
Megaspeed secured more than $4bn of Nvidia chips, The New York Times reported. US agents suspected it of smuggling some of them into China. Megaspeed has denied the diversion allegations.
Nvidia banned all sales and shipments to Megaspeed in June 2025, a spokesman told The Wall Street Journal.
“Any leakage is very frustrating”
Bessent linked the leakage to President Donald Trump’s limit on the Nvidia chips China may receive. Asked if he was frustrated by the delays over Megaspeed, he said:
“I am frustrated when President Trump made it very clear that China should not receive any Nvidia chips above H100s.”
“And so any leakage is very frustrating,” he said. It “hurts our great companies in the AI race [and] gives the Chinese an advantage.”
Huang had pushed Washington to ease limits on exporting advanced AI chips to China. In December 2025, Trump said Nvidia could sell its H200 chips to approved Chinese customers. The US would take a percentage of the sales.
“Commerce has the pen”
Bessent said Treasury, the Pentagon, the State Department and the US Trade Representative had all backed listing Megaspeed. The entity list is the Commerce Department’s trade blacklist. It cuts companies off from US technology. Megaspeed is not on it.
“They were in favor of putting Megaspeed on the entity list for months, but Commerce has the pen,” Bessent said. “You will have to ask them about their internal processes.”
His remarks came two days after an Axios report. It said Bessent had pressed Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick over Megaspeed in the White House Situation Room. Commerce spokeswoman Kristen Eichamer said the two had “no such conversation”. Asked about it on Friday, Bessent said:
“We don’t repeat conversations in the Situation Room.”
Commerce did not immediately respond to CNBC about Bessent’s remarks. A Commerce spokesperson told Semafor:
“Treasury and Commerce have a great working relationship.”
Commerce halted its Megaspeed probe in 2025 after Nvidia’s lawyer contacted its agents, the Times reported. The Senate Banking Committee has asked Huang and Lutnick to testify in December.

articles.title: Microsoft’s massive Outlook outage might be over
articles.text:
Service is recovering for Microsoft Outlook and 365 after an almost two-day outage impacting millions of users around the world. While some apps and features are still running in a degraded state on Friday morning, some people (including Verge staffers) reported that access to their emails had been restored, though the flow of Outlook mail might be delayed.
Microsoft’s massive Outlook outage might be over
Nearly a day after the global email outage started, Microsoft said the issue has been addressed and that it wasn’t related to a cyberattack or AI.
Just before noon on Friday, Microsoft said it’s seeing “broad recovery,” and that the problem “was a technical issue not related to cyber or AI / agents.”
We are deeply sorry for the disruption this incident has caused our customers and partners. We know the trust they place in our services and take that responsibility extremely seriously. We are seeing broad recovery and stability across our services.
This was a technical issue not related to cyber or AI / agents. The incident was introduced by an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade that surfaced following a recent network change. We have addressed the underlying issue and continue to restore service to remaining customers and regions.
Given the scale of demand, we restored services gradually, validating stability at each stage. While this took longer, it helped ensure a stable restoration.
We will provide a full post-incident report once our review is complete.
Senior Verge correspondent Tom Warren reports that according to his sources, the outage is linked to Azure VNet config changes. Microsoft has said that it hasn’t found any evidence of the outage being connected to “malicious activity,” and that a full report will be shared after the issues are mitigated. In a statement reported by Sky News tech correspondent Rowland Manthorpe, Microsoft described the outage as a “technical issue,” and says it isn’t related to “cyber, AI/agents, DDOS, etc.”
The scope of the outage also affected features in other Microsoft services, including SharePoint Online, Teams, Copilot AI, and 365 apps.
Update, November 13th, 2:15PM ET: Added the latest information from Microsoft.

articles.title: OpenAI wants ChatGPT Wallet to be ‘safe and easy to use’ for agents
articles.text:
OpenAI has launched ChatGPT Wallet, which lets its dots AI agents buy things for users without seeing their card details. The company built it with American Express, Mastercard and Visa, it said in its announcement on Friday.
Wallet starts in the US, for ChatGPT Pro subscribers aged 18 and over with eligible US-issued cards. OpenAI said it is starting small to learn from real-world use.
A security check for every purchase
Users add a card once. Before each purchase, they review the items, the total and the card. They then approve it with a check such as Face ID or a fingerprint scan. Each approval creates a record of what the user allowed the agent to buy.
After approval, the payment network issues a payment token. It stands in for the real card, with its own card number, security code and expiry date. The business and the agent never see the actual card details, OpenAI said.
Users keep their card’s rewards and its protections for eligible disputes, such as a defective item. Businesses keep control of pricing, delivery, returns and customer service.
“Our goal here is to really focus on merchants and our network partners and start building out a really great foundation that’s safe and easy to use,” Chaya Nayak, who leads product for monetization and payments at OpenAI, told CNBC’s Ashley Capoot.
OpenAI is not taking a cut of purchases for now, CNBC reported. Over time, OpenAI expects users to hand purchases to their agent entirely. They would set limits on spending, categories or time periods.
Sites that block agents
OpenAI said some websites may block purchases by agents without meaning to. Risk systems can also flag legitimate agent purchases as fraud, which leads to declines or cancellations.
To help, it published a playbook for businesses. It covers letting ChatGPT agents through firewalls, uploading product feeds and setting up business profiles in ChatGPT. OpenAI is also working with fraud firms Forter, Riskified, Sardine and Signifyd, and with payment providers Adyen, Checkout.com and Stripe.
United Airlines said on Wednesday it will block agents from booking tickets. Amazon stops them buying on its platform, CNBC reported. Schwab and JPMorgan are blocking AI agents from moving customer money.
OpenAI tried checkout in ChatGPT before. It launched an Instant Checkout feature in autumn 2025 and quickly moved away from it, CNBC reported. Visa tested 22 models as shoppers this month. They failed 42.8% of the time.
Luke Gebb, who heads global innovation at American Express, said the small launch is deliberate.
“It just makes sense to watch it, start it in a contained environment, and then keep rolling from there,” Gebb told CNBC.
Walmart lets agents shop through agent profiles with their own spending limits.
